(3.11)

Here, the interface between
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{L}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
is given by the stacking of the identity surface of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
and the canonical boundary of
\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{L}
.
The topological line at the intersection is a non-genuine line on the canonical boundary of
\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{L}
, which is labeled by an object of
\mathcal{A}^{\text{rev}}_{l}
due to (
3.10
).
If we gauge the
L^{\text{diag}}
symmetry on the left side, we obtain an interface between
(\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{L})/L^{\text{diag}}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
We denote this interface by
\mathfrak{I}_{0}
.
Since the
L^{\text{diag}}
surfaces become invisible after the gauging, the configuration (
3.11
) gives rise to a non-genuine line on
\mathfrak{I}_{0}
attached to
D_{2}^{l}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
This shows that the surface
D_{2}^{l}
for
l\in L
can end on
\mathfrak{I}_{0}
, and the non-genuine lines attached to
D_{2}^{l}
are labeled by objects of
\mathcal{A}^{\text{rev}}_{l}
.

On the other hand, the surface
D_{2}^{k}
for
k\in K
cannot end on
\mathfrak{I}_{0}
if
k
is not in
L
.
This means that the interface
\mathfrak{I}_{0}\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{k}
, which is the fusion of
\mathfrak{I}_{0}
and
D_{2}^{k}
, is not connected to
\mathfrak{I}_{0}
if
k
is not in
L
.
12
12

12

Two interfaces are said to be connected if and only if there exists a genuine line between them.

The interfaces
\mathfrak{I}_{0}\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{k}
and
\mathfrak{I}_{0}\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{k^{\prime}}
are connected if and only if
k
and
k^{\prime}
are in the same right
L
-coset in
K
.
Therefore, the connected components of the interfaces between
(\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{L})/L^{\text{diag}}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
are labeled by right
L
-cosets in
K
.
We choose
\mathfrak{I}_{i}:=\mathfrak{I}_{0}\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{k_{i}}
as the representative of each connected component, where
k_{i}
is the representative of a right
L
-coset.
Then, by construction, the topological lines at the junction of
\mathfrak{I}_{i}
,
\mathfrak{I}_{j}
, and
D_{2}^{k}
are labeled by objects of
\mathcal{A}^{\text{rev}}_{k_{i}kk_{j}^{-1}}
.
This agrees with the defining property (
3.4
) of the topological boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
.
Thus, we conclude that
(\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{L})/L^{\text{diag}}
agrees with
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
, i.e., (
3.9
) holds.

3.2
Genuine and Non-Genuine Lines on the Boundary

In this subsection, we discuss the category of non-genuine lines on
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
attached to the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}\in\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})
.
13
13

13

The Drinfeld center
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})
is described in detail in
[
48
]
.

Genuine lines can be regarded as a special case of non-genuine lines where
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}
is trivial.
As in section
3.1
, we suppose that
\mathcal{A}
is faithfully graded by
L\subset K
.

The non-genuine lines attached to
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}
are labeled by 1-morphisms between the identity surface on
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
and
F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})
, where
F:\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})\to{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}
is the bulk-to-boundary functor for
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
.
Namely, the non-genuine lines form a 1-category

\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}}(F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}),\mathcal{A}).

(3.12)

The bulk-to-boundary functor
F
is given by

F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})=\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})\otimes\mathcal{A}=\bigoplus_{k^{\prime}\in[k]}n_{k^{\prime}}D_{2}^{k^{\prime}}\otimes\mathcal{A}.

(3.13)

Here,
Forg
denotes the forgetful functor from
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})
to
2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda}
, and
n_{k^{\prime}}
is some non-negative integer.
The right
\mathcal{A}
-module structure on
F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})
is given by the right multiplication of
\mathcal{A}
, while the left
\mathcal{A}
-module structure is given by using the half-braiding of
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}
as follows:

\displaystyle\mathcal{A}\otimes F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})=\mathcal{A}\otimes\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})\otimes\mathcal{A}

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\text{half-braiding of ${\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}$}}

\displaystyle\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})\otimes\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A}

(3.14)

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\text{tensor product of $\mathcal{A}$}}

\displaystyle\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})\otimes\mathcal{A}=F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}).

The category (
3.12
) is non-vanishing if and only if
[k]\cap L
is not empty.
To see this, we consider the following equivalence of semisimple 1-categories:
14
14

14

In general, there is an equivalence of semisimple 1-categories
\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}}(\mathcal{A}\otimes X\otimes\mathcal{A},M)\cong\text{Hom}_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda}}(X,M)
for any
X\in 2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda}
and any
M\in{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}

[
69
]
.

\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}}(\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A},F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}))\cong\text{Hom}_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda}}(D_{2}^{e},F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}))\cong\mathop{\vphantom{\bigoplus}\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{837404}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{728180}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{555233}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{500623}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}}\displaylimits_{l\in[k]\cap L}\mathsf{Vec}^{\boxplus n_{l}\text{rank}(\mathcal{A}_{l^{-1}})}.

(3.15)

The second equivalence follows from eqs. (
3.2
) and (
3.13
).
The above equation implies that
F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})
contains a simple direct summand connected to
\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A}
if and only if
[k]\cap L
is not empty.
Here, we note that
\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A}
is a simple object of
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}
that is connected to the unit object
\mathcal{A}
.
15
15

15

It is shown in
[
69
]
that for an algebra object of the form
\mathcal{A}=\mathsf{Vec}_{H}^{\nu}\in 2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda}
, the object
\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{A}
is simple in
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}
. The same proof applies to more general algebra object
\mathcal{A}
as long as
\mathcal{A}_{e}
is fusion as we assume in the main text.

Therefore, (
3.15
) also implies that
F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})
contains a simple direct summand connected to
\mathcal{A}
if and only if
[k]\cap L
is not empty.
Hence, the category (
3.12
) is non-vanishing if and only if
[k]\cap L
is not empty.

The above result shows that the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}
can end on the boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
if and only if
[k]
contains an element of
L
.
In other words, only the surfaces
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[l]}
for some
l\in L
can end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
.
This is consistent with the physical interpretation (
3.9
) that
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
is obtained by gauging the diagonal
L
symmetry of
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{L}
.

The case of non-anomalous abelian
L
.

Let us describe the category of non-genuine lines in more detail.
For simplicity, we suppose that
\lambda
is trivial, in which case we have
\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]})=\bigoplus_{k^{\prime}\in[k]}D_{2}^{k^{\prime}}
.
In addition, we also suppose that the subgroup
L\subset K
is abelian.

We first notice that the category of non-genuine lines can be decomposed as

\displaystyle\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K})_{\mathcal{A}}}(F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}),\mathcal{A})

\displaystyle\cong\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{L})_{\mathcal{A}}}(\mathop{\vphantom{\bigoplus}\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{837404}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{728180}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{555233}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{500623}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}}\displaylimits_{l_{i}\in[k]\cap L}D_{2}^{l_{i}}\otimes\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})

(3.16)

\displaystyle\cong\mathop{\vphantom{\bigoplus}\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{837404}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{728180}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{555233}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{500623}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}}\displaylimits_{l_{i}\in[k]\cap L}\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{L})_{\mathcal{A}}}(D_{2}^{l_{i}}\otimes\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A}).

The first equivalence follows from the fact that there is no non-zero 1-morphism between
\mathcal{A}
and
D_{2}^{k^{\prime}}\otimes\mathcal{A}
if
k^{\prime}
is not in
L
.
The second equivalence follows from the fact that
D_{2}^{l}\otimes\mathcal{A}
for
l\in L
is by itself an
(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})
-bimodule in
2\mathsf{Vec}_{L}\subset 2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}
.
If we forget the
L
-grading,
D_{2}^{l_{i}}\otimes\mathcal{A}
is equivalent to
\mathcal{A}
as an
(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})
-bimodule.
Therefore, the direct summand
\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{L})_{\mathcal{A}}}(D_{2}^{l_{i}}\otimes\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})
is a subcategory of the category
\text{End}_{\mathsf{Bimod}(\mathcal{A})}(\mathcal{A})
of
(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})
-bimodule endofunctors of
\mathcal{A}
.
More specifically,
\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{L})_{\mathcal{A}}}(D_{2}^{l_{i}}\otimes\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})
is the category of
(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})
-bimodule functors that shift the grading by
l_{i}
.
Recalling that
\text{End}_{\mathsf{Bimod}(\mathcal{A})}(\mathcal{A})
is equivalent to the Drinfeld center of
\mathcal{A}

[
75
]
, we find

\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{L})_{\mathcal{A}}}(D_{2}^{l_{i}}\otimes\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})\subset\text{Hom}_{\mathsf{Bimod}(\mathcal{A})}(\mathcal{A})\cong\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}).

(3.17)

Under the equivalence
\text{Hom}_{\mathsf{Bimod}(\mathcal{A})}(\mathcal{A})\cong\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
, objects of
\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{L})_{\mathcal{A}}}(D_{2}^{l_{i}}\otimes\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})
correspond to objects of
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
whose underlying objects in
\mathcal{A}
are graded by
l_{i}
.
Thus, we have an equivalence

\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{L})_{\mathcal{A}}}(D_{2}^{l_{i}}\otimes\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})\cong\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})_{l_{i}},

(3.18)

where
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})_{l_{i}}
denotes the full subcategory of
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
consisting of objects whose underlying objects in
\mathcal{A}
have the grading
l_{i}
.
16
16

16

When
\mathcal{A}
is graded by an abelian group
L
, the Drinfeld center
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
is also graded by
L
.

Plugging the above equation into (
3.16
) leads us to

\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K})_{\mathcal{A}}}(F({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}),\mathcal{A})\cong\mathop{\vphantom{\bigoplus}\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{837404}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{728180}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{555233}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{500623}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}}\displaylimits_{l_{i}\in[k]\cap L}\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})_{l_{i}}.

(3.19)

This shows that the non-genuine lines attached to
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[k]}
are labeled by objects of
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})_{l_{i}}
for
l_{i}\in[k]\cap L
.

3.3
Non-Genuine Point Defects on the Boundary

In this subsection, we consider the non-genuine point-like defects on
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
attached to the bulk genuine line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
, where
R\in\mathsf{Rep}(K)
is a representation of
K
.
In particular, we show that
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
can end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
if and only if
\kappa(R)\in\mathsf{Rep}(L)
contains the trivial representation.
Here,
\kappa:\mathsf{Rep}(K)\to\mathsf{Rep}(L)
is the forgetful functor, that is,
\kappa(R)
for
R\in\mathsf{Rep}(K)
is
R
viewed as a representation of
L
.

We first recall the definition of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}\in\text{End}_{\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[e]})

[
48
]
.
The underlying 1-morphism of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
is given by

\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R})=\text{id}_{D_{2}^{e}}^{\oplus\text{dim}R}\in\text{End}_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda}}(D_{2}^{e}).

(3.20)

The half-braiding of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
and
D_{2}^{k}\in 2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda}
is given by

\begin{split}\hbox to114.21pt{\vbox to92.46pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 0.2pt\lower 10.67459pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke=#000000} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill=#000000} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width=0.4pt} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} {{}}{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}
{}{{}}{}
{}{}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width=0.8pt} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\lxSVG@setdash{0.8pt,2.0pt}{0.0pt}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-dasharray={0.8pt,2.0pt},stroke-dashoffset=0.0pt} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{}\lxSVG@stroke\lxSVG@drawpath@unclipped{M 78.74 64.57 L 78.74 78.74}{fill:none} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces
\lxSVG@closescope {}{{}}{}
{}{}
{}{}
{}{}
{}{}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill=#000000} \lxSVG@stroke@opacity{0.2}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-opacity=0.2} \lxSVG@fill@opacity{0.2}\lxSVG@begingroup@{fill-opacity=0.2} {}\lxSVG@fillstroke\lxSVG@drawpath@unclipped{M 0 62.99 L 125.98 62.99 L 157.48 94.49 L 31.5 94.49 L 0 62.99}{} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces
\lxSVG@closescope {}{{}}{}

(3.21)

where
R(k)\in\text{End}_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda}}(\text{id}_{D_{2}^{k}}\otimes\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}),\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R})\otimes\text{id}_{D_{2}^{k}})\cong\text{End}(\mathbb{C}^{\text{dim}R})
is the representation matrix of
R
.

If we push
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
onto the boudnary
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
, it becomes a boundary line
F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R})
, where
F
is the bulk-to-boundary functor:

F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R})=\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R})\otimes\text{id}_{\mathcal{A}}\in\text{End}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}}(\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[e]})\otimes\mathcal{A}).

(3.22)

The line
F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R})
is an
(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})
-bimodule 1-endomorphism of
\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[e]})\otimes\mathcal{A}\cong\mathcal{A}
.
The right
\mathcal{A}
-module 1-morphism structure on
F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R})
is trivial, while the left
\mathcal{A}
-module 1-morphism structure is given by using the half-braiding (
3.22
) as follows:

(3.24)

Now, we consider the point-like defects between
F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R})
and
F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R^{\prime}})
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
.
These point-like defects form a vector space

\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}}(F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}),F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R^{\prime}})).

(3.25)

Any element of this vector space is of the form

f\otimes\text{id}_{\text{id}_{\mathcal{A}}}:\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R})\otimes\text{id}_{\mathcal{A}}\to\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R^{\prime}})\otimes\text{id}_{\mathcal{A}},

(3.26)

where
f
is a 2-morphism from
\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R})
to
\text{Forg}({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R^{\prime}})
in
2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda}
.
The 2-morphism
f
must satisfy

(3.27)

so that
f\otimes\text{id}_{\text{id}_{\mathcal{A}}}
is an
(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})
-bimodule 2-morphism.
Since the half-braiding
R_{\mathcal{A}}
is given by (
3.24
), the above equation reduces to

f\circ R(l)=R^{\prime}(l)\circ f,\qquad\forall l\in L.

(3.28)

Namely,
f
is an intertwiner between
R
and
R^{\prime}
viewed as representations of
L
.
Therefore, we find

\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}}(F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}),F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R^{\prime}}))\cong\text{Hom}_{\mathsf{Rep}(L)}(\kappa(R),\kappa(R^{\prime})).

(3.29)

In particular, when
R^{\prime}=\text{triv}^{K}
is the trivial representation of
K
, we have

\text{Hom}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})_{\mathcal{A}}}(F({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}),\text{id}_{\mathcal{A}})\cong\text{Hom}_{\mathsf{Rep}(L)}(\kappa(R),\text{triv}^{L}).

(3.30)

This implies that
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
can end on the boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
if and only if
\kappa(R)
contains the trivial representation of
L
.
This result is consistent with the physical interpretation of
\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{A}}
in terms of stacking and gauging.

3.4
Interfaces

Let us describe the interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}
between
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
in terms of (bi)module 2-categories.
We first consider the topological boundary
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}^{\text{fold}}
obtained by folding the bulk TFT.
By construction, we have

\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}^{\text{fold}}=(\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{H^{\text{diag}}})/(H^{\text{diag}})^{\text{diag}}.

(3.31)

The notations used in the above equation are as follows.

•

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
is the Dirichlet boundary of the folded TFT

\overline{\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})}\boxtimes\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})\cong\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})\,,

(3.32)

where
\overline{\varpi}\pi
is defined by

\overline{\varpi}\pi((g_{1},x_{1}),(g_{2},x_{2}),(g_{3},x_{3}),(g_{4},x_{4})):=\varpi(g_{1},g_{2},g_{3},g_{4})^{-1}\pi(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},x_{4})

(3.33)

for all
g_{1},g_{2},g_{3},g_{4}\in G
and
x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in H/N
.

•

H^{\text{diag}}=\{(h,p(h))\mid h\in H\}
is a subgroup of
G\times H/N
, where
p:H\to H/N
is the canonical projection.

•

\mathcal{A}
is a
G\times H/N
-graded
\overline{\varpi}\pi
-twisted fusion category, which is faithfully graded by
H^{\text{diag}}
.

•

\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{H^{\text{diag}}}
is an anomalous
H^{\text{diag}}
-symmetric TFT with an anomaly
(\overline{\varpi}\pi)|_{H^{\text{diag}}}^{-1}
.
We note that
\overline{\varpi}\pi
restricted to
H^{\text{diag}}
can be written as

\overline{\varpi}\pi((h_{1},p(h_{1})),(h_{2},p(h_{2})),(h_{3},p(h_{3})),(h_{4},p(h_{4})))=(\varpi^{-1}p^{*}\pi)(h_{1},h_{2},h_{3},h_{4}),

(3.34)

which means that
\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{H^{\text{diag}}}
can be regarded as an
H
-symmetric TFT with anomaly
\varpi p^{*}\pi^{-1}
.

•

(H^{\text{diag}})^{\text{diag}}
is the diagonal
H^{\text{diag}}
subgroup of
(G\times H/N)|_{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}}\times H^{\text{diag}}|_{\mathfrak{T}_{\mathcal{A}}^{H^{\text{diag}}}}
.

Due to the results in section
3.1
, the boundary
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}^{\text{fold}}
defined by (
3.31
) is labeled by a
(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
-module 2-category

{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})\,.

(3.35)

By unfolding the TFT
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
, we obtain the corresponding interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}
between
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
.
From the unfolded picture,
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}
is labeled by a
(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi},2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
-bimodule 2-category
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
.
Here, the left
2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi}
-action
\vartriangleright:2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi}\times{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})\to{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
is given by

D_{2}^{g}\vartriangleright M:=M\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}},\qquad\forall M\in{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi}),

(3.36)

where
\vartriangleleft
on the right-hand side is the right action of
2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\overline{\varpi}}
on
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
.
On the other hand, the right
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-action on
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
is simply given by restricting the right
2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi}
-action to
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
.

From section
3.2
, the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[(g,x)]}
of the folded TFT
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
can end on
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}
if and only if
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[(g,x)]}={\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[(h,p(h))]}
for some
h\in H
.
After the unfolding procedure, a non-genuine line attached to
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[(h,p(h))]}
becomes an intersection of a bulk surface and
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}
.
The surface on the left side of the interface is
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[h]}
, while that on the right side is
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[p(h)]}
:

(3.37)

Here,
\mathcal{Z}(G,\varpi)
is the abbreviation of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})
and
\mathcal{Z}(G,\varpi)^{\text{bop}}
is
\mathcal{Z}(G,\varpi)
with the opposite braiding.
The second equality of (
3.37
) follows from the braided equivalence

\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})^{\text{bop}}\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\overline{\varpi}}):{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[h]}\mapsto\overline{{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[h]}}

(3.38)

where
\overline{{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[h]}}
is the dual of
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[h]}
.
Equation (
3.37
) implies that
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[n]}
for
n\in N
can end on
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}
from the left, while no surfaces can end from the right.

Furthermore, due to section
3.3
, the bulk lines
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R_{G}\otimes R_{H/N}}
of the folded TFT
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
can end on
\mathcal{I}^{\text{fold}}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}
if and only if
\kappa(R_{G}\otimes R_{H/N})\in\mathsf{Rep}(H^{\text{diag}})
contains the trivial representation.
The orthogonality relation of characters implies that
\kappa(R_{G}\otimes R_{H/N})
contains the trivial representation of
H^{\text{diag}}
if and only if the following condition holds:

\sum_{h\in H}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits[R_{G}(h)]\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits[R_{H/N}(p(h))]\neq 0.

(3.39)

When
R_{H/N}
is trivial, the above condition reduces to

\sum_{h\in H}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits[R_{G}(h)]\neq 0.

(3.40)

This condition is satisfied if and only if
\kappa(R_{G})\in\mathsf{Rep}(H)
contains the trivial representation of
H
.
On the other hand, when
R_{G}
is trivial, the above condition reduces to

\sum_{h\in H}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits[R_{H/N}(p(h))]=|N|\sum_{x\in H/N}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits[R_{H/N}(x)]\neq 0.

(3.41)

This condition is satisfied if and only if
R_{H/N}
is trivial.
The above result shows that after the unfolding,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R_{G}}
can end on
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}
from the left if and only if
\kappa(R_{G})\in\mathsf{Rep}(H)
contains the trivial representation, while no lines can end from the right.
We emphasize that neither surfaces nor lines can end on
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}
from the right.
17
17

17

More precisely, only the condensation defects can end from the right.

(3.42)

Here, the boundary on the left-hand side is labeled by a right
2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi}
-module 2-category
\mathcal{M}
.
Collapsing the region occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})
gives us a topological boundary of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
.
This boundary is labeled by a right
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-module 2-category
\mathcal{M}\boxtimes_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi}}{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
.

For concreteness, we consider the case where the original boundary of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})
is the Dirichlet boundary.
The corresponding module 2-category
\mathcal{M}
is the regular module

\mathcal{M}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi}.

(3.43)

In this case, the boundary obtained by the club quiche construction (
3.42
) is labeled by a right
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-module 2-category

2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi}\boxtimes_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi}}{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})\cong{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi}).

(3.44)

In general, this 2-category is decomposable as a module 2-category over
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
.

Let us decompose
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
into the direct sum of indecomposable
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-module 2-categories.
To this end, we first notice that
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
can be decomposed as a semisimple 2-category as follows:

{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})=\mathop{\vphantom{\bigoplus}\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{837404}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{728180}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{555233}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{500623}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}}\displaylimits_{w\in H\backslash G}\mathop{\vphantom{\bigoplus}\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{837404}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{728180}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{555233}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{500623}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}}\displaylimits_{x\in H/N}{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{(w,x)}.

(3.45)

Here,
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{(w,x)}
is a connected sub-2-category that contains
\mathcal{A}\otimes D_{2}^{(g_{w},x)}
for
g_{w}\in w
and
x\in H/N
, where
g_{w}
is a fixed representative of
w
.
The right
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-action on
\mathcal{A}\otimes D_{2}^{(g_{w},x)}\in{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
is given by

(\mathcal{A}\otimes D_{2}^{(g_{w},x)})\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{x^{\prime}}=\mathcal{A}\otimes D_{2}^{(g_{w},xx^{\prime})},\qquad\forall x^{\prime}\in H/N.

(3.46)

In particular, the action of
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
does not change
w\in H\backslash G
, while it acts transitively on
x\in H/N
.
This implies that
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{(w,x)}
and
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{(w^{\prime},x^{\prime})}
are sub-2-categories of the same indecomposable
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-module 2-category if and only if
w=w^{\prime}
.
Therefore, we obtain the following decomposition as a right
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-module 2-category

{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})=\mathop{\vphantom{\bigoplus}\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{837404}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{728180}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{555233}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{500623}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}}\displaylimits_{w\in H\backslash G}{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{w},

(3.47)

where we defined

{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{w}:=\mathop{\vphantom{\bigoplus}\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{837404}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{728180}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{555233}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{500623}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}}\displaylimits_{x\in H/N}{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{(w,x)}.

(3.48)

Since
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{w}
is an indecomposable module 2-category over
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
, there exists an
H/N
-graded
\pi
-twisted fusion category
\tilde{\mathcal{A}}
such that

{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{w}\cong{}_{\tilde{\mathcal{A}}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})

(3.49)

as a
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-module 2-category.
We note that
\tilde{\mathcal{A}}
is faithfully graded by the trivial group
\{e\}
because
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{w}
has as many connected components as
|H/N|
.
18
18

18

In general, the number of connected components of
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{K}^{\lambda})
is
|K|/|L|
if
\mathcal{A}
is faithfully graded by
L\subset K
.

Therefore, we have
\tilde{\mathcal{A}}=\tilde{\mathcal{A}}_{e}
.
To find
\tilde{\mathcal{A}}
, we consider the endomorphism 1-category of a simple object

\text{End}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})_{w}}(\mathcal{A}\otimes D_{2}^{(g_{w},x)})\cong\mathcal{A}_{e}^{\text{rev}},\qquad\text{End}_{{}_{\tilde{\mathcal{A}}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})}(\tilde{\mathcal{A}}\otimes D_{2}^{x})\cong\tilde{\mathcal{A}}_{e}^{\text{rev}}.

(3.50)

The above equation implies that
\tilde{\mathcal{A}}_{e}
must be Morita equivalent to
\mathcal{A}_{e}
.
In particular, we can choose
\tilde{\mathcal{A}}_{e}=\mathcal{A}_{e}
.
19
19

19

The choice of
\tilde{\mathcal{A}}
is not unique because
{}_{\tilde{\mathcal{A}}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
depends only on the Morita equivalence class of
\tilde{\mathcal{A}}
.

Thus, (
3.47
) leads to the following decomposition of a
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-module 2-category:

{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})\cong{}_{\mathcal{A}_{e}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})^{\boxplus|H\backslash G|}.

(3.51)

We note that
{}_{\mathcal{A}_{e}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
is equivalent to
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
as a
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-module 2-category.
Here,
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
does not act on
\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
, which is the 2-category of left
\mathcal{A}_{e}
-module categories.
Thus, the above equation can also be written as

{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})\cong(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e}))^{\boxplus|H\backslash G|}.

(3.52)

For later use, we denote the
i
th component of the right-hand side as
(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e}))_{i}
.
The equivalence (
3.52
) maps objects as

\mathcal{A}\otimes D_{2}^{(hg_{i},p(h)x)}\mapsto(D_{2}^{x}\boxtimes\mathcal{A}_{(h,p(h))^{-1}})_{i},

(3.53)

where
g_{i}
is the representative of a right
H
-coset in
G
.

Physically, the topological boundary labeled by
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
is the stacking of the Dirichlet boundary of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
and the 3d TFT
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
, cf. (
3.9
).
Therefore, (
3.52
) implies

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}^{G,\varpi}\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\mathcal{A})}=(\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}^{H/N,\pi}\boxtimes\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e}))^{\boxplus|H\backslash G|},

(3.54)

where
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}^{G,\varpi}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}^{H/N,\pi}
denote the Dirichlet boundaries of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
.

Implementation of the symmetry.

Let us consider the symmetry on the boundary obtained by the club quiche construction.
We will mainly focus on the case of the Dirichlet boundary, and briefly comment on the case of more general boundaries.

As we discussed above, if we start from the Dirichlet boundary of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})
, the club quiche construction gives us the direct sum (
3.54
) of the Dirichlet boundaries of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
, stacked with the 3d TFT
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
.
The symmetry on this boundary is described by the multifusion 2-category

\displaystyle(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})^{*}_{{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})}

\displaystyle=\mathsf{Fun}_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}}({}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi}),{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi}))

(3.55)

\displaystyle\cong\text{Mat}_{|H\backslash G|}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\Sigma\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})).

Here,
\Sigma\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
denotes the condensation completion of
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})

[
76
,
77
]
, which is monoidally equivalent to
\mathsf{Mod}(\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e}))

[
76
]
, the 2-category of
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
-module categories.
On the other hand, by construction, the boundary also has the symmetry described by
2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi}
, which is implemented by a monoidal 2-functor

\Phi:2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi}\to\text{Mat}_{|H\backslash G|}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\Sigma\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})).

(3.56)

In what follows, we determine this monoidal 2-functor at the level of objects.

Formally, the 2-functor
\Phi
is given by

\Phi(D_{2}^{g})=\Psi(-\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}}),

(3.57)

where
-\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}}
is a
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
-module 2-functor from
{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi})
to itself, and
\Psi
denotes the monoidal equivalence in (
3.55
).
The equivalence
\Psi
is given by the composition of the following equivalences:

\displaystyle\penalty\displaystyle\mathsf{Fun}_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}}({}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi}),{}_{\mathcal{A}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G\times H/N}^{\overline{\varpi}\pi}))

(3.58)

\displaystyle\overset{\psi_{1}}{\cong}\mathsf{Fun}_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}}\left(\mathop{\vphantom{\bigoplus}\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{837404}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{728180}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{555233}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{500623}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}}\displaylimits_{i}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e}))_{i},\penalty\ \mathop{\vphantom{\bigoplus}\mathchoice{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{837404}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{728180}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{555233}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}{\vbox{\hbox{\resizebox{500623}{}{$\boxplus$}}}}}\displaylimits_{j}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e}))_{j}\right)

\displaystyle\overset{\psi_{2}}{\cong}\text{Mat}_{|H\backslash G|}\left(\mathsf{Fun}_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e}),\penalty\ 2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e}))\right)

\displaystyle\overset{\psi_{3}}{\cong}\text{Mat}_{|H\backslash G|}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{Bimod}(\mathcal{A}_{e})).

The first equivalence
\psi_{1}
follows from (
3.52
), the second equivalence
\psi_{2}
follows in an obvious way, and the last equivalence
\psi_{3}
follows from

\displaystyle 2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{Bimod}(\mathcal{A}_{e})

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathsf{Fun}_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e}),\penalty\ 2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e}))

(3.59)

\displaystyle X\boxtimes M

\displaystyle\mapsto\quad(X\otimes-)\boxtimes(M\boxtimes_{\mathcal{A}_{e}}-).

The fusion 2-category
\mathsf{Bimod}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
is monoidally equivalent to
\Sigma\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})

[
78
,
79
]
.

Let us now compute
\Psi(-\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}})
by using (
3.58
).
First, we recall that the functor
-\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}}
maps objects as

\mathcal{A}\otimes D_{2}^{(hg_{i},p(h)x)}\xmapsto{-\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}}}\mathcal{A}\otimes D_{2}^{(hg_{i}g^{-1},p(h)x)}=\mathcal{A}\otimes D_{2}^{(hh_{ij}g_{j},\penalty\ p(h)x)}.

(3.60)

Here, we used the decomposition
g=g_{j}^{-1}h_{ij}^{-1}g_{i}
, where
g_{i}
and
g_{j}
are the representatives of right
H
-cosets in
G
and
h_{ij}\in H
.
We note that the decomposition of
g
is unique for any
g_{i}
.
The above equation combined with (
3.53
) implies that the functor
\psi_{1}(-\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}})
maps objects as

(D_{2}^{x}\boxtimes\mathcal{A}_{(h,p(h))^{-1}})_{i}\xmapsto{\psi_{1}(-\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}})}(D_{2}^{p(h_{ij}^{-1})x}\boxtimes\mathcal{A}_{(hh_{ij},p(hh_{ij}))^{-1}})_{j}.

(3.61)

Furthermore, the equivalence
\psi_{2}
maps this functor to a matrix whose components take values in the functor category
\mathsf{Fun}_{2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e}),2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{LMod}(\mathcal{A}_{e}))
.
The
(j,i)
-component of the matrix
\psi_{2}(\psi_{1}(-\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}}))
is given by

D_{2}^{x}\boxtimes\mathcal{A}_{(h,p(h))^{-1}}\xmapsto{\psi_{2}(\psi_{1}(-\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}}))_{ji}}D_{2}^{p(h_{ij}^{-1})x}\boxtimes\mathcal{A}_{(hh_{ij},p(hh_{ij}))^{-1}}.

(3.62)

We note that each column of this matrix has only one non-zero entry because
(h_{ij},g_{j})
is uniquely determined by
(g,g_{i})
.
Finally, the equivalence
\psi_{3}
maps the above matrix to another matrix whose components take values in
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\mathsf{Bimod}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
.
Due to (
3.59
), the
(j,i)
-component of the new matrix is given by

\psi_{3}(\psi_{2}(\psi_{1}(-\vartriangleleft D_{2}^{g^{-1}})))_{ji}=D_{2}^{p(h_{ij}^{-1})}\boxtimes\mathcal{A}_{(h_{ij},p(h_{ij}))^{-1}}.

(3.63)

Via the monoidal equivalence
\mathsf{Bimod}(\mathcal{A}_{e})\cong\Sigma\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})

[
78
,
79
]
, the
(\mathcal{A}_{e},\mathcal{A}_{e})
-bimodule
\mathcal{A}_{(h_{ij},p(h_{ij}))}
corresponds to the invertible object
D_{2}^{h_{ij}}\in\Sigma\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
, which implements the (possibly anomalous)
H
symmetry of the stacked TFT
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
.
Thus, we find

\Phi(D_{2}^{g})_{ji}=D_{2}^{p(h_{ij}^{-1})}\boxtimes D_{2}^{h_{ij}^{-1}}.

(3.64)

We note that the matrix
\Phi(D_{2}^{g})
satisfies
\Phi(D_{2}^{g})\Phi(D_{2}^{g^{\prime}})\cong\Phi(D_{2}^{gg^{\prime}})
as expected due to
h_{ij}^{-1}=g_{j}gg_{i}^{-1}
.

Before concluding this section, we mention that the boundary conditions other than the Dirichlet boundary can be obtained by gauging a separable algebra
\mathcal{B}\in 2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi}
on the Dirichlet boundary of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})
.
Equivalently, these boundaries can be obtained by gauging the separable algebra
\Phi(\mathcal{B})\in 2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}\boxtimes\Sigma\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}_{e})
after squashing the region occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G}^{\varpi})
in the club quiche.
Such boundaries will be studied in later sections of this paper for various concrete examples.

4
Gapless Phases from
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
DW Theory

To illustrate the general framework developed so far, consider
G={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
which is a simple, yet still non-trivial example. We will determine the gapless interfaces, both minimal and non-minimal, from the DW for
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
.
A summary of the transitions from minimal interfaces is shown in table
4
. For the reader interested in the general abelian groups, see appendix
B
.

The subgroups are
H=1,{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
and we furthermore have

H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{n},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{n}\,,\quad H^{4}({\mathbb{Z}}_{n},U(1))=0\,,

(4.1)

so the reduced topological orders are all without twist, i.e.
\pi=0
.
The gapped phases have
H=N
and are given as follows, using the notation that Neu
(A)
corresponds to gauging
A
on the Dirichlet BC:

\displaystyle H=N=1:

\displaystyle\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}

(4.2)

\displaystyle H=N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2},\ \omega\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}:

\displaystyle\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},\omega)}

\displaystyle H=N={\mathbb{Z}}_{4},\ \omega\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}:

\displaystyle\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4},\omega)}\,.

The interfaces to non-trivial TOs are as follows:

\displaystyle H={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,\

\displaystyle N=1\,,\

\displaystyle\omega

\displaystyle\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}:

\displaystyle\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})

\displaystyle H={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\,,\

\displaystyle N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2},\

\displaystyle\omega

\displaystyle\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}:

\displaystyle\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})

(4.3)

\displaystyle H={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\,,\

\displaystyle N=1,\

\displaystyle\omega

\displaystyle\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}:

\displaystyle\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}})\,.

The various choices are distinguished in terms of the cocyle
\omega
that governs the associators of lines on the interface. The case of
H=G
,
N=1
and trivial
\omega
yields the trivial interface, while for non-trivial
\omega
it describes an SPT-stacking interface.

These minimal condensable algebras/interfaces can be put into a partial order, that is depicted by a Hasse diagram as shown in figure
5
.
We will denote the simple objects in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}})
as

\displaystyle e^{p}

\displaystyle\equiv{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e^{p}}\,,

\displaystyle m^{p}

\displaystyle\equiv{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m^{p}}\,,

\displaystyle p

\displaystyle\in\{0,1,2,3\}\,.

(4.4)

The condensable algebras are shown in figure
5
, where arrows denote inclusion. The maximal algebras determined gapped boundary conditions of the SymTFT and were discussed in
[
1
]
.

\langle 1\rangle
({\mathbb{Z}}_{4},1,1)
\langle e^{2}\rangle
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},1,1)
\;\;\langle e^{2}\rangle^{\omega}
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},1,{\omega})
\langle m^{2}\rangle
({\mathbb{Z}}_{4},{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},1)
\langle m^{2}\rangle^{\omega}
({\mathbb{Z}}_{4},{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},\omega)
\langle m^{2}\rangle^{\omega^{2}}
({\mathbb{Z}}_{4},{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},{\omega^{2}})

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
in the reduced TO have non-trivial associator given by the SPT 3-cocycle, which we indicated as
\omega
.

4.3
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}
-Symmetric Phase Transitions

We can change the symmetry boundary so that the symmetry is
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}
:

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}}:\qquad\mathcal{S}={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\,.

(4.13)

Here, all
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m^{i}}
can end on the symmetry boundary, whereas
the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e^{p}}
become the 1-form symmetry generators
D_{1}^{e^{p}}
.

\langle e^{2}\rangle
Condensed Interface.

In this case none of the surfaces that can end on the symmetry boundary have endpoints/lines on the interface.

To apply the KT transformation, we compactify the interval with
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}})
. The
Q_{2}^{M}
surface in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
can be connected to
Q_{2}^{m^{2}}
in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}})
across the interface, and can thus end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
. The
Q_{1}^{E}
line in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
becomes
Q_{1}^{e}
line in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}})
, which generate the 1-form symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
. However, the
D_{1}^{e^{2}}
line that generate the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\subset{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}
1-form symmetry is isomorphic to a trivial line since it can end on a local operator in the IR. Therefore, we obtain the
\mathfrak{B}_{m,\omega}
boundary for the
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
reduced TO after compactifying the
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}})
interval.

The KT transformation of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
trivial phase is the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}
trivial phase. The KT transformation of the
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{0}
phase is a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB phase, which is equivalent to the Toric Code topological order. There is an unbroken
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry that comes from compactfying the
e^{2}
lines and acts trivially on the anyons. We simply denote this gapped phase as
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{0}
. The KT transformation of the
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{1}
phase is another
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB phase, which is equivalent to the double semion topological order. There is also an unbroken
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry that acts trivially in the IR. We denote this gapped phase as
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{1}
.

(4.14)

(4.15)

Here
\mathcal{L}^{m^{2}}
is a non-trivial line.
We first discuss the boundary of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
obtained by compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}})
. The
Q_{2}^{M}
surface in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
can be connected to
Q_{2}^{m}
or
Q_{2}^{m^{3}}
in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}})
across the interface, and can thus end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
. The
Q_{1}^{E}
line in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
becomes
Q_{1}^{e^{2}}
line in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}})
, and generates the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\subset{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
. Additionally, the
Q_{2}^{m^{2}}
surface can end on both the symmetry boundary and the interface, and it becomes a line
\mathcal{L}^{m^{2}}
with non-trivial associators coming from
\omega
. The
\mathcal{L}^{m^{2}}
line is charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
generated by
D_{1}^{e}
line. In summary, the boundary of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
is given by

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{e}\boxtimes\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{\omega|_{N}}}{({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},\omega)},

(4.16)

where
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry fractionalizes on the bosonic anyon in
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{\omega|_{N}}
. We note that the boundary of the reduced TO can also be written as

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}={\mathfrak{B}_{m}\boxtimes\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{{4}})_{\omega}\over{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}}\,,

(4.17)

which matches the expression for general abelian groups in Eq. (
B.37
). In this expression, gauging the diagonal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry removes extra lines in
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{Z_{4}})_{\omega}
. The confined lines, such as
\mathcal{L}^{m}
and
\mathcal{L}^{m^{3}}
, are then attached to the end of
Q_{2}^{M}
surface in the reduced TO.

We now discuss the KT transformation to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}
gapped phases for
\omega=0
. The KT transformation of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
trivial phase is the untwisted
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB phase, which we denote as
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{0}
. Note that there is an unbroken
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry generated by the
D_{1}^{e}
line. The KT transformation of the
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{0}
phase is the untwisted
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}
SSB phase, which we denote as
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})_{0}
. The KT transformation of the
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{1}
phase is the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}
SSB phase twisted by
2\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4},U(1))
, which we denote as
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})_{2}
.

If we input
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
, the KT transformed theory is given by

\begin{split}\hbox to164.06pt{\vbox to32.67pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 46.80064pt\lower-16.33351pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke=#000000} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill=#000000} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width=0.4pt} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} {{}}{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}
{{}}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\hbox{\hbox{{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} {{}{}{{
{}{}}}{
{}{}}

{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
1-form symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
. There is a local operators
\mathcal{O}
, which come from compactifying the
e^{2}
line extended between
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and the interface. Therefore, we find that boundary of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
reduced TO is given by

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=(\mathfrak{B}_{m})_{0}\oplus(\mathfrak{B}_{m})_{1}.

(4.20)

The KT transformation takes a theory with
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry and output a theory with
\left({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\right)^{\beta}
symmetry. We now discuss the KT transformation of the gapped phases with
\omega=0
. The KT transformation of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
SSB phase is the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
SSB phase, in which there is a unbroken
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry. The KT transformation of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
trivial phase is the untwisted
\left({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\right)^{\beta}
SSB phase, which we denote as
\left({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\right)^{\beta}\text{SSB}_{0}
. There are 2 vacua exchanged by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry, and each vacuum realizes the untwisted
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{0}
theory. Moreover, the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry fractionalized on the
e
anyon due to the mixed anomaly. The KT transformation of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
SPT phase is the twisted
\left({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\right)^{\beta}
SSB phase, which we denote as
\left({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\right)^{\beta}\text{SSB}_{1}
. There are 2 vacua exchanged by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry, and each vacuum realizes the twisted
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{1}
theory, which is equivalent to the double semion topological order. Moreover, the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry fractionalized on the bosonic
s\bar{s}
anyon due to the mixed anomaly.

(4.21)

The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry acts by exchanging the two gauged Ising sectors. If

and

, this theory describes the phase transition between the

phases. If

and

, this theory describes the transition between the

\langle m^{2}\rangle
Condensed Interface.

The
Q_{1}^{E}
maps to
Q_{1}^{e^{2}}
and ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
. The
Q_{2}^{M}
becomes
D_{2}^{m}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
. In addition, the
Q_{2}^{m^{2}}
surface can end on both the symmetry boundary and the interface, and it becomes a line
\mathcal{L}^{m^{2}}
, which braids non-trivially with the 1-form symmetry generator
D_{1}^{e}
. We thus find that the boundary of the
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
reduced TO is given by

\mathfrak{B}_{e}\boxtimes\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{\omega|_{N}}\,.

(4.22)

. The KT transformation of the

phase. The KT transformation of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
trivial phase is the untwisted symmetry enriched
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB phase, in which the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry fractionalized on the
e
anyon due to the mixed anomaly. We simply denote this phase as
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{0}
. The KT transformation of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
trivial phase is the stacking of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
SPT and the untwisted symmetry enriched
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB phase. Similarly, the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry fractionalized on the
e
anyon. We denote this phase as
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})_{0}\boxtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\text{-SPT}
.

(4.25)

Non-minimal
\langle m^{2}\rangle
Condensed Interface.

Here we describe the non-minimal interface on which the
m^{2}
surface condensed. This is described by
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
,
N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
and
\mathcal{A}
, a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
graded fusion category. The category of lines on this interface forms the MTC

\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})=\bigoplus_{h\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}}\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{h}\,,

(4.26)

where the grading is provided by the
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})
line
D_{1}^{e}
obtained from the projection of
Q_{1}^{e}
on the interface. The properties of this interface are depicted as follows

(4.29)

The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
symmetry has been spontaneously broken down to
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
and each vacua support a topological order described by the MTC
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})
. This gapless theory describes the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
SSB transition between the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetric MTC and the MTC in which the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
symmetry is completely broken.

A concrete example is obtained where
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})
is the Toric Code topological order. In this case,
\mathcal{A}
is the Tambara-Yamagami category of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
, which is a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
graded fusion category. The trivial component is
\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
and the non-trivial grading component consists of a non-invertible object
\{\sigma\}
. The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
symmetry acts non-faithfully on the Toric Code, in which the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
subgroup acts as the automorphism that exchanges
e
and
m
anyons. Therefore,
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
is the double Ising topological order generated by the anyons
\{1,\sigma,\psi\}\times\{1,\bar{\sigma},\bar{\psi}\}
. The gapless theory (
4.29
) describes the phase transition from the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry enriched Toric Code, in which the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
symmetry has been partially broken down to
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
, to the Toric Code with no 0-form symmetry. If we choose
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}=\text{Ising}
, each sector of the transition in (
4.29
) is described by the 3d Ising CFT in which the twisted sector line from the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry defect is decorated by the non-trivial anyons in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{m^{2}}=\{\sigma,\bar{\sigma},\sigma\bar{\psi},\psi\bar{\sigma}\}
.

(4.34)

The genuine lines are described by
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{m^{2}}
, which is a degenerate MTC since the
D_{1}^{e^{2}}
line in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}}
braids trivial with all other lines. Moreover, lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{m}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{m^{3}}
are attached to
Q_{2}^{M}
surface after compactification. The non-minimal BC of the reduced TO can be obtained as follows. First, we gauge the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
symmetry generated by the
D_{1}^{e^{2}}
in
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
:

\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}=\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)},

(4.35)

so that the the lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{m}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{m^{3}}
are confined. With
D_{1}^{e^{2}}
condensed,
\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}
is then a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetric MTC. Now the non-minimal BC of the reduced TO is given by

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{e}\boxtimes\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}.

(4.36)

4.5.3
\mathbb{G}^{(2)}=\left({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\right)^{\beta}
Phase Transitions from Non-Minimal Interfaces

Finally we discuss the
\mathbb{G}^{(2)}=\left({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}\right)^{\beta}
symmetric phase transitions by choosing
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})}
with non-minimal interfaces.

Non-minimal
\langle e^{2}\rangle
Condensed Interface.

In this case the club quiche results in an non-minimal BC of the reduced TO

5.1
The SymTFT

We begin by very briefly reviewing the
S_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory.
We present the group
S_{3}
as

S_{3}=\big\langle a\,,b\ \big|\ a^{3}=b^{2}=1\,,bab=a^{2}\,\big\rangle\,.

(5.1)

The SymTFT which plays a central role in our analysis of symmetries and phases is the (3+1)d
S_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory
[
30
]
.
Let us briefly recap the topological defects in the SymTFT.
For details see
[
2
]
.
In general, the (co-dimension-2 and higher) topological defects of the (3+1)d
G
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory are organized as
[
48
]

\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G})=\boxplus_{[g]}2\mathsf{Rep}(H_{g})\,,

(5.2)

where
[g]
are conjugacy classes in
G
and
H_{g}
is the centralizer of a representative element in
[g]
.
Since,
S_{3}
has three conjugacy classes
[\text{id}]\,,[a]=\{a\,,a^{2}\}
and
[b]=\{b\,,ab\,,a^{2}b\}
with
H_{\text{id}}=S_{3}\,,H_{a}={\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
and
H_{b}={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
, we obtain

\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})=2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\boxplus 2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})\boxplus 2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})\,.

(5.3)

Up to condensations, each 2-category
2\mathsf{Rep}(H_{g})
has a single simple (non-condensation) object, i.e. topological 2d surface defect. We denote these simple objects by

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}\,,\ {\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}\,,\ {\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\,,

(5.4)

labeled by the conjugacy classes of
S_{3}
.
The topological surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}
is the transparent or identity surface. The geniune topological lines of the SymTFT form the category
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})

{1\rm End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\,.

(5.5)

Here
P
denotes the 1-dimensional irreducible representation of
S_{3}
that transforms with the sign
(-1)^{j}
under
a^{i}b^{j}
and
E
denotes the 2-dimensional irreducible representation whose representation space is spanned by vectors
v_{1}
and
v_{2}
that transform as

a:v_{i}\longmapsto\omega^{i}v_{i}\,,\qquad b:v_{1}\longleftrightarrow v_{2}\,,

(5.6)

with
\omega=\exp(2\pi i/3)
.
Meanwhile the lines on
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
form

\begin{split}{1\rm End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]})&=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[a],1}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[a],\omega}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[a],\omega^{2}}\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})\,,\\
{1\rm End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]})&=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[b],+}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[b],-}\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})\,.\end{split}

(5.7)

The phase between obtained by unlinking a genuine line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
wrapping a circle
S_{1}

and a surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}
wrapping a sphere
S_{2}
is

\chi_{R}([g])\,.

(5.8)

5.2
Symmetries and Gapped Boundary Conditions

The topological boundary conditions (BCs) of such a (3+1)d SymTFT can be divided into two classes: minimal and non-minimal.
These were studied in detail in
[
2
]
.
Here we summarize them for completeness.
The minimal BCs are those for which every topological line defect of the boundary arises by projecting a topological line defect of the bulk.
Equivalently, this means that there exist topological local operators on the boundary that connect each boundary line to some bulk line.
The non-minimal BCs are those which have additional boundary lines not satisfying this property.
On a non-minimal BC, any line that isn’t obtainable by the boundary projection of a bulk line, is necessarily remotely detectable
22
22

22

This statement is a corollary of the fact that non-modular braided fusion categories are boundary conditions for non-invertible Crane-Yetter-Kauffman TQFTs.
.

Minimal boundary Conditions.

A convenient way to obtain any minimal boundary condition is to start with the Dirichlet boundary condition, and gauge a sub-group
H
of the
S_{3}
0-form symmetry on it.
There is an additional choice of discrete torsion
\omega\in H^{3}(H,U(1))
in gauging
H
, which can be understood as stacking an
H
-SPT and then gauging
[
80
]
.
The boundary condition obtained by gauging
H
with discrete torsion
\omega
is the
H
-Neumann boundary condition denoted as

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(H),\omega}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}}{(H,\omega)}\,.

(5.9)

Let us describe the structure of these boundary conditions in terms of how the bulk topological defects of the SymTFT end on them, as this will be important for later purposes.

•

Dirichlet Boundary Condition.
Each SymTFT line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
for
R\in\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
has
\text{dim}(R)
ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
which we denote as
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R,i}
with
i=1,\dots,\text{dim}(R)
.
We denote this as

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}\Bigg|_{\text{Dir}}=\left\{\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R,i}\ \Big|\ i=1,\dots,\text{dim}(R)\right\}\,.

(5.10)

Each bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}
splits into a direct sum of surfaces
D_{2}^{g}
for
g\in[g]
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, which fuse according to the group multiplication in
S_{3}
.
These are the generators of the
S_{3}
0-form symmetry on this boundary.
More specifically, the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}
has twisted sector ends
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{g}
for all
g\in[g]
, where the line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{g}
is in the twisted sector of the
D_{2}^{g}
defect on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
We denote this as

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}\Bigg|_{\text{Dir}}=\left\{(D_{2}^{g}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{g})\quad\Big|\quad g\in[g]\ \right\}\,.

(5.11)

The topological operators
\{\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R,i}\}
transform as an
R
-multiplet under the
S_{3}
symmetry.

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}

{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}

Neumann
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
Boundary Conditions.

These boundary conditions are obtained by gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
with discrete torsion
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
.
Upon such a gauging,
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{P}
which was charged under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, goes to the twisted sector of a dual
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry, which we denote as
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
.

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),\omega}=\left(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{P}\right)\,.

(5.18)

The ends
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}
of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, can be decomposed into linear combinations
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,\pm}=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\pm\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}

with
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}
being uncharged and charged under
D_{2}^{b}
.
Therefore upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{b}
, one obtains

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),\omega}=\left\{\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}\,,(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-})\right\}\,.

(5.19)

The surfaces
D_{2}^{a}
and
D_{2}^{a^{2}}
are mapped to one another upon conjugation by
D_{2}^{b}
, therefore

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),\omega}=\left\{(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{A})\right\}\,,

(5.20)

where
D_{2}^{A}
is an indecomposable defect on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),\omega}
obtained from
D_{2}^{a}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{2}}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
This non-invertible non-condensation defect has fusion rules

D_{2}^{A}\otimes D_{2}^{A}=D_{2}^{\text{id}}\oplus\frac{D_{2}^{\text{id}}}{D_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}}\,.

(5.21)

Similarly,
D_{2}^{ab}
and
D_{2}^{a^{2}b}
are mapped to one another upon conjugation by
D_{2}^{b}
therefore

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),\omega}=\left\{\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\,,(D_{2}^{A}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab})\right\}\,,

(5.22)

where
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{Ab}
is an indecomposable twisted sector line on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),\omega}
obtained from
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}b}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
The line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}
has F-symbols given by
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,U(1))
.
In summary, this boundary carries a symmetry corresponding to the 2-representations of the 2-group generated by a (non-condensation) non-invertible 0-form symmetry generator
D_{2}^{A}
and a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form generator
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
.
This
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),\omega}
boundary condition is depicted as

Neumann
S_{3}
Boundary Conditions.

This boundary condition is obtained by gauging the full
S_{3}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
The SymTFT lines
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
end on twisted sector local operators

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}(S_{3}),\omega}=(D_{1}^{R}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R})\,,

(5.24)

where the
D_{1}^{R}
generate a
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
1-form symmetry.
The SymTFT surfaces end on single untwisted sector lines

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}(S_{3}),\omega}=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[g]}\,.

(5.25)

The line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[g]}
has a braiding phase of
\chi_{R}([g])
with
D_{1}^{R}
.
The lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[g]}
have F-symbols that are determined by
\omega\in H^{3}(S_{3},U(1))
and are precisely those of the
3d

S_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with topological action
\omega

[
81
]
.
All other symmetry defects on this boundary can be obtained as condensation defects constructed from the
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
lines.

\mathcal{Z}(S_{3})
(for surfaces). The reduced TO is

A condensable algebra
(H\,,N\,,\pi\,,\omega)
defines a topological interface between
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
.

and
N

\pi=0
in the following.
Consequently, the minimal interfaces in the
S_{3}

\left(H\,,N\,,\omega\right)
where

is a subgroup of
G
,

is a normal subgroup of
H
and
\omega\in H^{3}(H,U(1))
.
We will denote this interface as

\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\omega)}\,.

(5.27)

The different kinds of interfaces from
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
to
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N})
are summarized in Table
6
.
There are two kinds of non-trivial reduced TOs obtainable from
{\rm DW}(S_{3})
.

\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
and
\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
.
We now consider them in turn.

There are two classes of minimal interfaces between
\rm DW(S_{3})
and
\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})

5.3.1
Q_{2}^{[a]}
Condensed Interface

We
first consider an interface to DW
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
for which the only non-trivial defect that can end is
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
.
In terms of the aforementioned data, this corresponds to the choice
H=S_{3}
and
N={\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
.
For this choice the projection map

\kappa:\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\to\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
is just the identity, with a trivial kernel.
Therefore, we recover that none of the SymTFT lines can end on this interface.
The
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
surface can however end on this interface as
[a]\in H
.
The reduced topological order is

\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})\equiv\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})\,.

(5.28)

We will denote the non-trivial surface and line defects in the reduced TO as
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
respectively.
Since
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
braids non-trivially with
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
, it is confined on the interface.
In contrast,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
braids trivially with
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
and therefore can pass through the defect.
It becomes the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
of the reduced topological order.
Finally,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
becomes
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
in the reduced TO.
In summary, the map from defects on
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
to

\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
is

(5.29)

There is a further choice of discrete torsion valued in
(p,t)\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}=H^{3}(S_{3}\,,U(1))
when defining this interface.
We denote the end of the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
surface on
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}
and the line where the surfaces
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
meet on the interface as
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[b]m}
.
The choice of discrete
(p,t)
translates to F-symbols for the lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}
and
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{m[b]}
.
More specifically, these are precisely the F-symbols for the flux lines in the
(p,t)
twisted
S_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory
[
82
,
81
]
.

5.3.2
Q_{1}^{E}
Condensed Interface

Consider the interface where
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
can end, which also is an interface to DW
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
. This corresponds to the choice
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
and
N=1
. Therefore, we consider the projection

\kappa:\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\longrightarrow\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})\,,\qquad\kappa:({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E})\longmapsto({\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\text{id}}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e})\,.

(5.30)

This implies that
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
has a single end on this interface.
Meanwhile
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
gets confined as it braids non-trivially with
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
.
The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
becomes
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
in the reduced TO.
In summary, the map from defects on
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
to
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
is

(5.31)

The choice of discrete torsion
\omega
determines the F-symbols of the lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[b]m}
.

5.3.3
Q_{1}^{P}
Condensed Interface

There is a single class of minimal interfaces between
{\rm DW}(S_{3})
and
{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
.
This interface corresponds to the choice
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
and
N=1
.
Therefore, we consider the projection

\kappa:\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\longrightarrow\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})\,,\qquad\kappa:(D_{1}^{P}\,,D_{1}^{E})\longmapsto(D_{1}^{\text{id}}\,,D_{1}^{\omega}\oplus D_{1}^{\omega})\,.

(5.32)

This implies that
D_{1}^{P}
can end on this interface.
Furthermore, since
N=1
, none of the bulk surfaces in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
can end on the interface.
The reduced TO is
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})
.
Let us denote the topological lines and surfaces in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})
as
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e^{p}}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m^{q}}
respectively where
p,q=0,1,2
.
Since
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
is condensed on the interface and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\otimes{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}={\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
, there is an extra local operator on
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
.
Therefore this line splits as it passes through the interface.
In the reduced TO
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
becomes
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}\oplus Q_{1}^{e^{2}}
.

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
also passes through the interface as it braids trivially with
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
.
Moreover, it also splits as it can absorb
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
.
As a consequence in the reduced TO, this surface become
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m^{2}}
.
The surface,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
is confined on the interface as it braids non-trivially with
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
.

p\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},U(1))
.

p
translates to the associators of two lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]m}
and
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]m^{2}}
.

5.3.4
Hasse Diagram

Starting from a certain phase
\mathcal{P}
defined via a set of condensed charges
\mathcal{Q}_{\mathcal{P}}
, a further deconfined charge, i.e., an element of
\mathcal{Q}_{\mathcal{D}}
can be condensed without un-condensing any of the condensed charges.
Such an additional condensation produces a less gapless phase
\mathcal{P}^{\prime}
.
Specifically we mean that the number of dynamical pr deconfined generalized charges in
\mathcal{P}^{\prime}
is fewer than in
\mathcal{P}
.
A gapped phase is one where there are no deconfined charges.
Therefore one obtains a partial ordering on phases, given by the inclusion of algebras.
The complete set of condensable algebras along with the partial ordering can be conveniently organized into a Hasse diagram.
For
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
, the Hasse diagram has the form in figure
6
.

\langle 1\rangle
(S_{3},1,1)
\langle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}\rangle
(S_{3},{\mathbb{Z}}_{3},(p,t))
\;\;\langle{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\rangle
({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},1,{p})
\langle{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\rangle
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},1,t)
\langle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\rangle
(S_{3},S_{3},(p,t))
\langle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\rangle
({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},1,p)
\langle{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\rangle
(1,1,1)
\langle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\,,{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\rangle
({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},{t})

Figure 6
:
The set of condensable 2-algebras in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
has a partial ordering given by inclusion of algebras.
These algebras form a Hasse diagram depicted above.
Each box contains a condensable algebra, for which we provide generating objects and the data
(H,N,\omega)
.

5.4
Non-Minimal Interfaces

Non-minimal interfaces have the property that they contain line operators that are not obtainable via a boundary projection of a bulk SymTFT line.
Equivalently, there are boundary lines for which there is no topological local operator that connects them to a bulk line.
Non-minimal interfaces in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
are described by the datum
(H,N,\mathcal{A})
where
\mathcal{A}
is an
H
-graded fusion category.
Note that minimal interfaces are recovered by setting
\mathcal{A}=\mathsf{Vec}_{H}^{\omega}
.
Specifically, an interface labeled as
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\mathcal{A})}
has the property that the category of lines on it forms
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
.
There is a
\mathsf{Rep}(H)
worth of lines on this interface given by the boundary projection of lines in the SymTFT
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
via the functor

\kappa:\mathsf{Rep}(G)\longrightarrow\mathsf{Rep}(H)\,.

(5.34)

These lines can be used to grade
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
as

\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})=\bigoplus_{[h]}\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[h]}\,,

(5.35)

where the sum is over conjugacy classes in
H
.
Specifically the grading is given by the braiding of a line in
\mathsf{Rep}(H)
with the lines in
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
.
Any line in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[h]}
has a braiding of
\chi_{R}([h])
with a line
D_{1}^{R}
for
R\in\mathsf{Rep}(H)
.
Clearly,
\mathsf{Rep}(H)
is the Müger center of the grade
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}
.
Only the lines in the trivial grade
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}
are unattached to a bulk surface.
The lines in all other grades are attached to bulk surfaces.
For
h\in\ker(p)\cong N
, the lines
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[n]}
arise at the end of the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[n]}
surfaces in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G})
.
For
h\in{\rm im}(p)\cong H/N
, the lines
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[h]}
are attached to the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[h]}
surfaces in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{G})
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[p(h)]}
surfaces in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N})
.

Non-Minimal Interfaces from Non-Minimal Gauging.

Non-minimal interfaces between
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{n}})
for
n=2,3
can be obtained via a modification of the “folding and gauging approach.
Wherein, we stack the Dirichlet boundary condition of the folded theory
\overline{\rm DW(S_{3})}\boxtimes{\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{n})}
with an
H

\mathfrak{T}_{H}
to obtain

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}^{\mathfrak{T}_{H}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{H}\,.

(5.36)

The underlying category of lines of
\mathfrak{T}_{H}
is described by an MTC
\mathcal{M}
and
H
action is described via a
H
-crossed braided extension of
\mathcal{M}
, denoted as
\mathcal{M}_{H}^{\times}
.
In terms of the above defined
H
-graded fusion category
\mathcal{A}

\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})\,,

(5.37)

where
\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}}
is the identity grade.

\mathcal{A}
is the category of lines on the Dirichlet boundary of
\mathfrak{T}_{H}
, where the
H
-grading is given by the lines on the ends of
H
-condensation surfaces on the boundary.
Then we gauge
H^{\text{diag}}

We are abusing notation here as by
H^{\text{diag}}

H^{\text{diag}}
and the
H
symmetry action on
\mathfrak{T}_{H}
.
defined via
\mathcal{A}
(see section

) and unfold to obtain a non-minimal interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\mathcal{A})}

(5.38)

5.4.1
Non-Minimal Interfaces to
\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

There are two classes on non-minimal interfaces to the reduced TO
\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
, which are the non-minimal extensions of the interfaces with
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
condensed respectively. Let us describe these in turn

Non-minimal
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
Condensed Interface.

Recall that this interface corresponds to
H=S_{3}
and
N=1
.
Correspondingly, we stack an
S_{3}
-symmetric 3d TFT
\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
and subsequently gauge the diagonal
S_{3}
.
Let us denote the
S_{3}
crossed braided extension of
\mathcal{M}
as

\mathcal{M}^{\times}_{S_{3}}=\bigoplus_{g\in S_{3}}\mathcal{M}^{g}\,,

(5.39)

where the grade
\mathcal{M}^{g}
contains the topological line defects at the end of the condensation surface that implements the
g\in S_{3}
symmetry in
\mathfrak{T}
.
After gauging
S_{3}
, this grade combines with other grades in the
[g]
conjugacy class.
Moreover, these become untwisted topological line operators that are charged under the dual non-invertible
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
1-form symmetry.
Specifically, after gauging
S_{3}
, one obtains

\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[a]}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[b]}\,,

(5.40)

where

\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}=\frac{\mathcal{M}^{\text{id}}}{S_{3}}\,,\quad\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[a]}=\frac{\mathcal{M}^{a}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}}}{S_{3}}\,,\quad\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[b]}=\frac{\mathcal{M}^{b}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{ab}\oplus\mathcal{M}^{a^{2}b}}{S_{3}}\,.

(5.41)

Let us describe the physical meaning of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[g]}
in terms of defects on the interface, SymTFT and reduced TO.
On the interface,
\mathcal{I}^{\mathfrak{T}}_{(S_{3},{\mathbb{Z}}_{3},\mathcal{A})}
,
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}
forms a braided fusion category of lines that are unattached to any bulk surfaces either from the SymTFT or the reduced TO.
The Müger center of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}
is

\mathcal{Z}_{2}(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]})=\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\,.

(5.42)

Specifically, the lines that generate
\mathcal{Z}_{2}(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]})
are obtainable via the projection of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
onto the interface.
Next, the lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[a]}
are attached to the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
surface in
{\rm DW}(S_{3})
.
This is the non-minimal generalization of
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}
.
Finally, the lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[b]}
are attached to the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
surface in
{\rm DW}(S_{3})
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
surface in
{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
.
This is the non-minimal generalization of
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[b]m}
.
This interface can be depicted as

\begin{split}\hbox to139.83pt{\vbox to153.44pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 0.97763pt\lower-19.71414pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke=#000000} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill=#000000} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width=0.4pt} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} {{}}{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}
{}{{}}{}
{}{}

(5.43)

The associators and other remaining data of these lines are internal to
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}=\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
.

Non-minimal
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
Condensed Interface.

Following the same procedure, we now obtain minimal interface, on which the category of lines forms the MTC

\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})\,,

(5.44)

where
\mathcal{A}
is a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
graded fusion category.
In this case,
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
has an order 2 Bosonic line
D_{1}^{P}
obtained by the projection of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
.
This line provides a grading on
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
as

\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{p}\,,

(5.45)

such that the lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}}
braid trivially with
D_{1}^{P}
while the lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{p}
have a -1 braiding with
D_{1}^{P}
.

5.4.2
Non-Minimal Interfaces to
\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})

Non-minimal
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
Condensed Interface.

We now describe the non-minimal interface, on which the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
line can end.
This is described by
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
,
N=1
and
\mathcal{A}
a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
graded fusion category.
The category of lines on this interface forms the MTC

\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})\,.

(5.47)

In this case,
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
has a
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
category of lines obtained by projecting the
{\rm DW}(S_{3})
lines via the projection functor

\kappa:\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\longrightarrow\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})\,.

(5.48)

In particular, the lines
D_{1}^{\omega}
and
D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}
are obtained by the projection of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
.
The
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
lines provide a grading on
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})
as

\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})=\bigoplus_{h\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{h}\,,

(5.49)

such that the braiding of the lines in
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{h}
with
D_{1}^{\omega}
is
\exp\left\{2\pi ih/3\right\}
.
