(5.50)

5.5
Club Quiches

We now pick the symmetry boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
to be one of the minimal gapped boundaries of
{\rm DW}(S_{3})
such that the 2-category of defects on it determine the symmetry
\mathcal{S}
.
Then, upon inserting a topological interface (minimal or non-minimal) to a reduced TO and compactifying the interval occupied by the SymTFT
{\rm DW}(S_{3})
, one obtains a (possibly decomposable) boundary condition
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
of the reduced TO.
Let the symmetry carried by
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
be denoted as
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
.
We determine the 2-functor

\mathcal{F}:\mathcal{S}\longrightarrow\mathcal{S}^{\prime}\,,

(5.51)

for different choices of symmetry boundary and interface.

5.5.1
2\mathsf{Vec}(S_{3})
Symmetric Club Quiches

Consider
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, on which all the SymTFT lines can end.
This boundary carries an
S_{3}
0-form symmetry on it.
Now let us in turn choose various possible minimal interfaces

•

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
Condensed Interface:
As described previously, this is an interface to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
reduced TO.
Since
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
can end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
is connected to
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
across the interface, after compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
, we obtain a boundary condition
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
for the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
reduced TO on which
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
can end.
This is therefore the Dirichlet boundary condition.

The
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line in the
S_{3}
SymTFT gets confined on this interface and therefore becomes a line isomorphic to the identity line on compactifying the
S_{3}
SymTFT.
The
D_{2}^{a}
symmetry generating the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
subgroup of
S_{3}
has a twisted sector operator obtained from compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
with the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
surface stretched between the interface and symmetry boundary.
Specifically, after taking the club quiche one obtains two twisted sector lines

(D_{2}^{a}\,,\mathcal{L}^{a})\quad\text{and}\quad(D_{2}^{a^{2}}\,,\mathcal{L}^{a^{2}})\,.

(5.52)

These satisfy
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
fusion rules and their associator depends on
p
where
\omega=(p,t)\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\cong H^{3}(S_{3},U(1))

These are the properties of a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
SPT labeled by
p
.
The underlying 3d TFT corresponding to a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
SPT is simply the Trivial theory.

Let us finally describe the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
.
The
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
surface become the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
surface which ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
on a twisted sector line, attached to a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry defect.
This
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
defect has two relevant properties — (i) the end of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
is charged under it and (ii) it swaps the two ends of the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
surface which form a generalized 1-charge of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
.
Consequently after taking the club quiche, i.e., compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
, we find that the end of
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
is attached to a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
defect that satisfies the following two properties.
(i) the end of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
is charged under it and (ii) it swaps the twisted sector lines in (
5.52
).
The boundary condition is simply

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\mathfrak{B}_{e}\,.

(5.53)

Since the 3d TFT underlying an SPT is trivial, i.e., it does not have any non-identity defects, the symmetry category on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
is simply

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\,.

(5.54)

The club quiche furnishes a 2-functor mapping between the symmetry categories

\begin{split}\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}}\longrightarrow 2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\,,\end{split}

(5.55)

under which
\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{b})=D_{2}^{m}
and
\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{a})=D_{2}^{\text{id}}
.
The associators of
D_{2}^{m}
are modified by
t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
.

Non-minimal generalization.

Consider the non-minimal generalization of the interface
\mathcal{I}_{(S_{3},{\mathbb{Z}}_{3},\mathcal{A})}
, where
\mathcal{A}
is an
S_{3}
graded fusion category.
By picking
\mathcal{A}=\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}}^{\omega}
and viewing it as an
S_{3}
graded fusion category, we recover the minimal case.
Now let us consider a more general
S_{3}
graded algebra.
The corresponding interface was described previously.
The new non-minimal aspect of this interface is that it hosts an MTC of line defects which is

\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})=\bigoplus_{[h]}\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[h]}\,.

(5.56)

Among these, the lines in the grade
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}
are unattached to any SymTFT surface while lines in the remaining grades are attached to surfaces in the SymTFT or reduced TO.

Upon compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
, we obtain a non-minimal boundary condition
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
,
which hosts the genuine lines
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}=\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})
.
Furthermore, compactifying the SymTFT interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
provides
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
twist defect order parameters.

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
has a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry implemented by the parallel projection of
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
.
For reasons similar to the minimal case described above, the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
defect acts on the local operator at the end of the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
line and also implements a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
action on the topological order.
The boundary condition is identified as

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\frac{\left(\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{e}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}\boxtimes\frac{\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}\right)}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\rm diag}}\,.

(5.57)

The category of defects on this boundary is

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\ \boxtimes\ \Sigma(\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}}))

(5.58)

The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
0-form symmetry is realized as a condensation defect that
implements the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\subset S_{3}
symmetry of the MTC.
The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry is realized as the diagonal
D_{2}^{m}\otimes D_{2}^{\phi}
, where
D_{2}^{m}
is the non-trivial object in
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
, while
D_{2}^{\phi}
is the condensation defect implementing
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\subset S_{3}
symmetry.

•

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
Condensed interface:

This corresponds to an interface to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
reduced TO.
The SymTFT line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
has two ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and a single end on the interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\omega)}
.
After compactifying the interval occupied by the
S_{3}
SymTFT, we obtain a topological boundary condition

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
with three topological local operators

1\,,\quad\mathcal{O}^{1}\,,\quad\mathcal{O}^{2}\,,

(5.59)

and consequently the 2-category of defects on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
is a multifusion category that decomposes into a direct sum of 3 indecomposable fusion 2-categories.
The operators
\mathcal{O}^{j}
with
j=1,2
come from compactifying the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line extended between
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and the interface with the two possible choices of ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
.
Specifically, the local operator
\mathcal{O}^{j}
comes from fixing the end of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line to be
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,j}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E}
on the symmetry boundary and the interface respectively:

\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}\end{split}

(5.60)

The ends
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,j}
transform as a doublet in the
E
representation of the
S_{3}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}

D_{2}^{a}:\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,j}\longmapsto\omega^{j}\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,j}\,,\quad D_{2}^{b}:\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\longleftrightarrow\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}\,.

(5.61)

Requiring consistency between the fusion of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
and its ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and the interface imposes the operators to satisfy the following
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
fusion rules

\mathcal{O}^{1}\times\mathcal{O}^{2}=\mathcal{O}^{2}\times\mathcal{O}^{1}=1\,,\quad\left(\mathcal{O}^{1}\right)^{2}=\mathcal{O}^{2}\,,\quad\left(\mathcal{O}^{2}\right)^{2}=\mathcal{O}^{1}\,.

(5.62)

Therefore the components of multifusion category
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
are labeled by idempotents or projectors onto these components, which are obtained via a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
Fourier transform to be

\begin{split}\Pi_{j}=\frac{1+\omega^{j}\mathcal{O}^{1}+\omega^{2j}\mathcal{O}^{2}}{3}\,.\end{split}

(5.63)

After performing the club quiche, i.e, compactifying the interval occupied by the
S_{3}
SymTFT, one obtains the boundary condition

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{0}\ \oplus\ \left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{1}\ \oplus\ \left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{2}\,,

(5.64)

where
\mathfrak{B}_{e}
is the
e
-condensed or Dirichlet boundary condition of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
SymTFT.
The category of defects is multifusion category, that may be viewed as a 3-category whose objects are connected components.
The 2-category of endomorphisms of the
i^{\rm th}
component form the symmetry on
(\mathfrak{B}_{e})_{i}
which is
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
.
The 2-category of morphisms between the
i^{\rm th}
and
j^{\rm th}
components is the regular
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
module that is
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
.
Therefore we obtain

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}={\rm Mat}_{3}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})\,.

(5.65)

Here,
\text{Mat}_{n}(\mathcal{C})
denotes a multifusion 2-category whose objects are
n\times n
matrices with entries in a fusion 2-category
\mathcal{C}
.
Let us now describe the functor

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Vec}(S_{3})\longrightarrow{\rm Mat}_{3}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})\,.

(5.66)

The
S_{3}
action on the components of
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
is straightforwardly deduced from the linking action

\begin{split}\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{a})&=1_{01}\oplus 1_{12}\oplus 1_{20}\,,\\
\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{b})&=\left(D_{2}^{m}\right)_{00}\oplus\left(D_{2}^{m}\right)_{12}\oplus\left(D_{2}^{m}\right)_{21}\,,\end{split}

(5.67)

where
1_{ij}
is the invertible surface that has the the following linking action on the idempotents

1_{ij}\Pi_{k}=\delta_{jk}\Pi_{i}\,.

(5.68)

The fusion of surfaces satisfies

\begin{split}1_{ij}1_{kl}=\delta_{jk}1_{il}\,,\qquad\left(D_{2}^{m}\right)_{ij}=1_{ij}\otimes\left(D_{2}^{m}\right)_{jj}=\left(D_{2}^{m}\right)_{ii}\otimes 1_{ij}\,.\end{split}

(5.69)

From these it can be verified that
\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{a})
and
\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{b})
provide an
S_{3}
representation on the surfaces in
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
.
This choice of interface will correspond to gapless SSB phases upon completing the club quiche to a club sandwich.

Non-minimal generalization.

Now we consider the non-minimal generalization of the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
condensed interface.
This interface can be defined via a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
graded algebra
\mathcal{A}=\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}}\oplus\mathcal{A}^{p}
.
The category of lines on the interface is

\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{p}\,,

(5.70)

where
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}}
is a braided fusion category with center
\mathsf{Rep}(Z_{2})
generated by the interface projection of the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
.
While
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{p}
are the lines attached to
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
respectively.
Upon compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
, we again get a three component multifusion category.
The symmetry category on this boundary is

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}={\rm Mat}_{3}\left(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\ \boxtimes\ \Sigma[\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})]\right)\,.

(5.71)

The functor is very similar to the one described in (
5.67
) except with the replacement

\left(D_{2}^{m}\right)_{ij}\longrightarrow\left(D_{2}^{\phi m}\right)_{ij}\equiv\left(D_{2}^{m}\otimes D_{2}^{\phi}\right)_{ii}\otimes 1_{ij}\equiv 1_{ij}\otimes\left(D_{2}^{m}\otimes D_{2}^{\phi}\right)_{jj}\,,

(5.72)

where
\left(D_{2}^{\phi}\right)_{ii}
is a condensation defect that implements the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry on
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})
in the
i^{\rm th}
component.

•

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
Condensed interface:
This is an interface to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
reduced TO.
Since
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
can end on both the interface and the symmetry boundary, one obtains an addition local operator (denoted
\mathcal{O}
) after compactifying the interval occupied by the
S_{3}
SymTFT.

(5.73)

The topological local operator has the OPE
\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{O}=1
.
Therefore
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
is a multifusion 2-category with two components, such that the projectors onto these components are

\Pi_{0}=\frac{1+\mathcal{O}}{2}\,,\qquad\Pi_{1}=\frac{1-\mathcal{O}}{2}\,.

(5.74)

Next,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
has two local (untwisted) ends on symmetry boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
.
These become the ends for
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e^{2}}
after we compactify the interval occupied by the
S_{3}
SymTFT.
Therefore the boundary condition obtained after compactifying the SymTFT is

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{0}\ \oplus\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{1}\,.

(5.75)

The 2-category of topological defects on this boundary is

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}={\rm Mat}_{2}(2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}))\,.

(5.76)

The club quiche defines a 2-functor that prescribes the
\mathcal{S}
symmetry realization on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Vec}(S_{3})\longrightarrow{\rm Mat}_{2}(2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}))\,,

(5.77)

where

\begin{split}\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{a})&=\left(D_{2}^{m}\right)_{00}\oplus\left(D_{2}^{m^{2}}\right)_{11}\,,\\
\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{b})&=1_{01}\oplus 1_{10}\,.\\
\end{split}

(5.78)

Upon fixing a gapless physical boundary, this choice of interface would correspond to a gapless SSB phase with two dynamically disconnected sectors/universes.

Non-minimal generalization.

Now we consider the non-minimal generalization of the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
condensed interface.
This interface can be defined via a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
graded algebra
\mathcal{A}
.
The category of lines on the interface is

\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a}\ \oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a^{2}}\,,

(5.79)

where
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}}
is a braided fusion category with center
\mathsf{Rep}(Z_{3})
generated by the interface projection of the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
.
While
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a}
and
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a^{2}}
are the lines attached to
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m^{2}}
in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
respectively.
Upon compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
, we again get a two component multifusion category.
The symmetry category on this boundary is

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}={\rm Mat}_{2}\left(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}\ \boxtimes\ \Sigma[\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})]\right)\,.

(5.80)

The functor is very similar to the one described in (
5.78
) except with the replacement

\left(D_{2}^{m^{j}}\right)_{ii}\longrightarrow\left(D_{2}^{\phi^{j}m^{j}}\right)_{ii}\,,

(5.81)

where
\left(D_{2}^{\phi}\right)_{ii}
is a condensation defect that implements the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetry on
\mathcal{Z}(A^{\text{id}})
in the
i^{\rm th}
component.

5.5.2
2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
Symmetric Club Quiches

Now we describe the club quiches with the symmetry boundary chosen as

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}),p}\,.

(5.82)

These can be constructed by starting with the club quiches obtained with
2\mathsf{Vec}(S_{3})
symmetry and gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
sub-symmetry on the symmetry boundary.

•

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
Condensed Interface:

Let us consider the interface labeled by

H=S_{3}\,,\quad N={\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\,,\quad\omega=(p^{\prime},t^{\prime})\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}=H^{3}(S_{3},U(1))\,.

(5.83)

The
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
surface can end on both the symmetry boundary and the interface.
This surface has two untwisted ends on the symmetry boundary and one on the interface therefore after compactifying the interval occupied by the
S_{3}
SymTFT with the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
stretched between the interface and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
, we obtain condensed lines
\mathcal{L}^{a}
and
\mathcal{L}^{a^{2}}

(5.84)

These lines are charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
generated by
D_{1}^{\omega}
and
D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}
, which are obtained from the boundary projections of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
.
Furthermore, the
F
-symbols of these lines is given by

p-p^{\prime}\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},U(1))\,.

(5.85)

The
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
line can end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
.
Since
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
is attached to the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
line across the interface, this boundary condition becomes
a non-minimal Dirichlet boundary condition
\mathfrak{B}_{e}
of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
after compactifying the club quiche.

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}\in\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
becomes the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}\in\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
across the interface which further becomes a line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[b]}
in the twisted sector of the
D_{2}^{b}
(upto condensation).
This
D_{2}^{b}
symmetry defect acts as the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry on the
\mathfrak{B}_{e}
with the additional property that it also implements a charge conjugation
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry.

In summary, the category of defects on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
is

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{e}/{\mathbb{Z}}^{(0)}_{2}\ \boxtimes\ \mathfrak{T}_{\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}),p-p^{\prime}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1),\rm diag}}

(5.86)

where
\mathfrak{T}_{\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}),p-p^{\prime}}
is the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory whose topological action is given by
[p-p^{\prime}]\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},U(1))
.
The multifusion 2-category of defects on this boundary has the following structure.
There is a single topological local operator, i.e., it is fusion.
Upto condensations, there is a single non-trivial surface, which we denote as
D_{2}^{m}
.
The 1-endomorphisms of the identity object form a modular tensor category describing the lines of the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory.
We denote this MTC as
{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})_{p-p^{\prime}}
and its Karoubi completion
[
77
,
83
]
into a 2-category as

\Sigma\left({\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})_{p-p^{\prime}}\right)\,.

(5.87)

More precisely, the category of defects on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
form the 2-category

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\boxtimes\Sigma\left({\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})_{p-p^{\prime}}\right)\,.

(5.88)

The club quiche furnishes the functor

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})\longrightarrow 2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\boxtimes\Sigma\left({\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})_{p-p^{\prime}}\right)\,.

(5.89)

Under this functor,
D_{2}^{b}
maps to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
generator in
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
stacked with the charge conjugation condensation defect
[
26
]
in the Dijkgraaf-Witten theory.
While the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
generators are mapped to the to the topological Wilson lines in the Dijkgraaf-Witten theory.
Finally we note that the lines in the twisted sector of the 0-form
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry generators on this boundary have associators that are determined by the datum
t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,U(1))
on the interface.
Upon choosing a gapless physical boundary, this choice of interface will correspond to a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetric gapless phase where the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry is spontaneously broken, i.e., a gapless 1-form SSB.

Non-minimal generalization.

The non-minimal generalization of this gapless 1-form SSB phase can be described in terms of an
S_{3}
symmetric MTC
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})
that was obtained from the non-minimal
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
condensed interface and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
Upon gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
0-form subsymmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
one obtains a non-minimal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
SSB phase, denoted as
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}}\oplus\mathcal{A}^{a}\oplus\mathcal{A}^{a^{2}})
.
This 3d TFT theory has a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
left behind after the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
gauging.
We denote the condensation defect implementing this
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry as
D_{2}^{\phi}
.
Then the non-minimal symmetry category is

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\boxtimes\Sigma\left[\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}}\oplus\mathcal{A}^{a}\oplus\mathcal{A}^{a^{2}})\right]\,.

(5.90)

There is a 2-functor
\mathcal{F}:\mathcal{S}\to\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
which maps the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
generators to the (broken)
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
generators in
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}}\oplus\mathcal{A}^{a}\oplus\mathcal{A}^{a^{2}})
and the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
generator to
D_{2}^{m}\otimes D_{2}^{\phi}
.

•

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
interface:
With this choice of interface, the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line can end on both the interface and the symmetry boundary.
This line has two ends on the symmetry boundary.
After compactifying the interval occupied by the
S_{3}
SymTFT, one obtains local operators in the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
twisted sectors.

Non-minimal generalization.

Since the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
is trivial in this gapless phase, the minimal extension is rather straightforward.
It simply involves stacking with an
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}

{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
Condensed Interface:
For this choice,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
can end on both the symmetry boundary and the interface.
After compactifying the interval occupied by
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
, one obtains a local operator
\mathcal{O}
that is charged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form subsymmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
as in (
5.73
).
Furthermore,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
has two untwisted ends
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a}
and
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a^{2}}
on the symmetry boundary.
The
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
surface is connected to
D_{2}^{m}\oplus D_{2}^{m^{2}}
across the interface.
Therefore after compactifying the interval region occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}(S_{3}))
, we obtain the boundary condition

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\left(\mathfrak{B}_{m}\right)_{0}\ \oplus\ \left(\mathfrak{B}_{m^{2}}\right)_{1}\,.

(5.95)

The 2-category of topological defects on this boundary form

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}={\rm Mat}_{2}\left(2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})\right)\,.

(5.96)

The two components in this multifusion category correspond to the projectors

\Pi_{0}=\frac{1+\mathcal{O}}{2}\,,\quad\Pi_{1}=\frac{1-\mathcal{O}}{2}\,.

(5.97)

The 2-group symmetry is represented on this boundary via the functor

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})\longrightarrow{\rm Mat}_{2}\left(2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})\right)\,.

(5.98)

such that

\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{b})=1_{01}\oplus 1_{10}\,,\quad\mathcal{F}(D_{1}^{\omega})=(D_{1}^{e})_{00}\oplus(D_{1}^{e^{2}})_{11}\,.

(5.99)

Upon choosing a gapless physical boundary, this will correspond to a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
gapless SSB phase where
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
is spontaneously broken and therefore there are two gapless vacua related by
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
.

Non-minimal generalization.

In this case, one obtains a multifusion category, such that category of defects within each component is given by the Karoubi completion of a braided fusion category
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}}
descibed in (
5.79
) into a 2-category

\Sigma_{2}(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}})\,.

(5.100)

The full symmetry on the non-minimal boundary obtained after compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
is

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}={\rm Mat}_{2}\left(\Sigma_{2}(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}})\right)\,.

(5.101)

Then the functor
\mathcal{F}:\mathcal{S}\to\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
is again given by (
5.99
) where
(D_{1}^{e})_{ii}
denotes the generator of the Müger center of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}})
in the
i^{\rm th}
component.

5.5.3
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
Symmetric Club Quiches

We now move on to the club quiches obtained by considering the symmetry boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),t}\,.

(5.102)

•

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
Condensed Interface:

D_{2}^{A}
is trivialized as we get a condensed twisted sector order parameter after compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
.
The 2-category of defects on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
has a single component as none of SymTFT lines can end on both the interface and the symmetry boundary.
The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
in the reduced TO
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
continues across the interface as
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
which has a single untwisted end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
.
Therefore the boundary
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
is the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
condensed (or
\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
) boundary of the reduced TO with discrete torsion
t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\mathfrak{B}_{m,t}\,.

(5.103)

The symmetry
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
on this boundary is a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry which is corresponds to

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})\,.

(5.104)

The club quiche furnishes a monoidal 2-functor

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})\longrightarrow 2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})\,.

(5.105)

Such that

\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{A})\cong 2D_{2}^{\text{id}}\,,\quad\mathcal{F}(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}})=D_{1}^{e}\,.

(5.106)

Non-minimal generalization.

To obtain the non-minimal generalization, we start with the
S_{3}
symmetric TO
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})
obtained from taking the club quiche with
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
Then we gauge the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry on the symmetry boundary with the choice of discrete torsion
t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
.
This produces a non-minimal boundary condition of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{e}\ \boxtimes\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})}{({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)},t)}\,.

(5.107)

The category of defects on this boundary is

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=\Sigma\left(\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}\right)=\Sigma\left(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{0}\right)\,.

(5.108)

The Müger center of the braided fusion category
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{0}
is
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
generated by the boundary projection of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
.
We denote the corresponding defect in
\Sigma(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{0})
as
D_{1}^{e}
.
Also recall that there was a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetry implemented on
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})
24
24

24

Defined either via a choice of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
restriction of
\mathcal{A}
or the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
restriction of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\times}_{S_{3}}
.
.
Let us denote the corresponding
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
condensation defects as
D_{2}^{\phi_{a}}
and
D_{2}^{\phi_{a^{2}}}
.
These are exchanged by the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
action and therefore combine into a single non-invertible symmetry defect

D_{2}^{\phi_{A}}=\left(D_{2}^{\phi_{a}}\oplus D_{2}^{\phi_{a^{2}}}\right)/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,.

(5.109)

Now we are ready to describe the functor

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})\longrightarrow\Sigma(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{0})\,.

(5.110)

Under this functor

\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{A})=D_{2}^{\phi_{A}}\,,\qquad\mathcal{F}(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}})=D_{1}^{e}\,.

(5.111)

Finally, note that the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}\in\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
ends on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
on the category of lines
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}
whose associators have been modified by
t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
.

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
Condensed Interface:

The
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
line can end (and has a single end) on both the interface and the symmetry boundary.
Therefore are compactifying the interval occupied by
{\rm DW}(S_{3})
, we obtain an additional local operator
\mathcal{O}
on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
.
The fusion rules of
\mathcal{O}
are (see Sec 3.5.3 in
[
2
]
)

\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{O}=2+\mathcal{O}\,.

(5.112)

Since
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
has two local operators, the category of defects on it forms a multifusion 2-category with two components.
The projectors onto these components are the projectors

\Pi_{0}=\frac{2-\mathcal{O}}{3}\,,\qquad\Pi_{1}=\frac{1+\mathcal{O}}{3}\,.

(5.113)

We can describe the boundary condition
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
by directly gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetry on (
5.64
).
Since
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
acts within
(\mathfrak{B}_{e})_{0}
while it exchanges
(\mathfrak{B}_{e})_{1}
and
(\mathfrak{B}_{e})_{2}
, we obtain

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\frac{\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{0}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}\ \boxplus\ \left(\frac{(\mathfrak{B}_{e})_{1}\ \boxplus\ (\mathfrak{B}_{e})_{2}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}\right)\,,

(5.114)

The symmetry category on this boundary is a multifusion 2-category with two components.
The component labeled
0
(descending from
\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{0}
upon gauging) carries the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
, while the component labeled
1
(descending from
\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{1}\boxplus\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{2}
upon gauging) carries
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
.
Additionally there are morphisms between these two components given by
2\mathsf{Vec}
.
The interface defects between distinct components
i
and
j
are denoted as
B_{ij}
.
In summary, the symmetry category can be described by the matrix of 2-categories

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=\begin{pmatrix}2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})&2\mathsf{Vec}\\
2\mathsf{Vec}&2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\end{pmatrix}\,.

(5.115)

The club quiche determines a functor
\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})\to\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
, such that

\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{A})=B_{01}\ \oplus\ B_{10}\ \oplus\ 1_{11}\,,\qquad\mathcal{F}(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}})=(D_{1}^{e})_{00}\ \oplus\ D_{1}^{\text{id}}\,.

(5.116)

•

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
Condensed Interface:
After compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
, one obtains a
D_{1}^{\widehat{b}}
twisted order parameter, therefore the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
sub-symmetry is trivialized in this gapless phase.
There are no topological local operators on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
other than the identity.
The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
that goes to the
D_{2}^{A}
twisted sector on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
becomes
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m^{2}}
across the interface.
Therefore after collapsing the interface on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}

\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})
, i.e.,
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\mathfrak{B}_{m}
.
This boundary carries a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
0-form symmetry.

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})\longrightarrow 2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}\,,

(5.117)

such that

\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{A})=D_{2}^{m}\oplus D_{2}^{m^{2}}\,,\qquad\mathcal{F}(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}})\cong D_{1}^{\text{id}}\,.

(5.118)

Non-minimal generalization.

The category of lines on the non-minimal generalization of the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
condensed interface forms the modular tensor category

\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}=\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{1}\ \oplus\ \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a}\ \oplus\ \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{a^{2}}\,,

(5.119)

where
\mathcal{A}
is a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
graded fusion category.
The boundary condition obtained after compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
is

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{e}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(0)}\ \boxtimes\ \mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(0)}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}}\,,

(5.120)

where
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
is the 3d TFT whose underlying MTC is
\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A}^{\text{id}})
and
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetry action is defined via
\mathcal{A}
.
The 2-category of defects on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
is given by the Karoubi completion of
\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{[\text{id}]}
into a 2-category.

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=\Sigma(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}})\,.

(5.121)

Let us denote the condensation defects implementing the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
0-form on
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
as
D_{2}^{\phi_{a}}
and
D_{2}^{\phi_{a^{2}}}
.
Then the club quiche furnishes a functor

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})\longrightarrow\Sigma(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^{\text{id}})\,,

(5.122)

under which

\mathcal{F}(D_{1}^{\widehat{b}})\cong D_{1}^{\text{id}}\,,\qquad\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{A})\cong D_{2}^{\phi_{a}}\oplus D_{2}^{\phi_{a^{2}}}\,.

(5.123)

5.5.4
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
Symmetry

We now consider the symmetry boundary to be

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3}),\omega}\,,

(5.124)

which carries a
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
symmetry on it.
We will denote
\omega=(p,t)\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\cong H^{3}(S_{3},U(1))
.

•

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
Condensed Interface:

Consider the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
Condensed Interface labeled by
H=S_{3}
,
N={\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
and
(p^{\prime},t^{\prime})\in H^{3}(S_{3},U(1))
.
The
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
surface ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
on a untwisted line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[a]}
which is charged under (braids non-trivially with)
D_{1}^{E}
that generates the non-invertible
\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
1-form symmetry.
Therefore, this line is added to the symmetry category
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
.
The reduced TO after taking the club quiche is
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
.
The line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
in the reduced TO connects to
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
that ends on a local operator attached to
D_{1}^{P}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
.
Therefore upon compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
,
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e}
has a twisted sector end attached to
D_{1}^{e}
which generates a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry.
The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
in the reduced TO becomes the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[b]}
surface in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
that can end on a single untwisted line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[b]}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
whose
F
symbols are determined by
t-t^{\prime}\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
.
We identify the boundary condition after taking the club sandwich as

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\frac{{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})_{p-p^{\prime}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{B}_{e}}{({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0),\rm diag},t-t^{\prime})}\,.

(5.125)

Here we have stacked
{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})_{p-p^{\prime}}
, the 3d
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with topological action
p\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},U(1))
on the Dirichlet boundary condition and gauged the diagonal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
that acts as charge conjugation on
{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})_{p-p^{\prime}}
and via
D_{2}^{m}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
The category of all line defects on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
form

\frac{{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})_{p-p^{\prime}}}{({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)},t-t^{\prime})}\cong{\rm DW}(S_{3})_{(p-p^{\prime},t-t^{\prime})}\,.

(5.126)

However some of these are attached to bulk surfaces in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
.
Specifically the lines that are charged under
\mathsf{D}_{1}^{e}
are attached to bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
.
Therefore the symmetry category on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
is obtained by removing the lines that braid non-trivially with
D_{1}^{e}
from
{\rm DW}(S_{3})_{(p-p^{\prime},t-t^{\prime})}
.
We can give
{\rm DW}(S_{3})_{(p-p^{\prime},t-t^{\prime})}
a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
grading

{\rm DW}(S_{3})_{(p-p^{\prime},t-t^{\prime})}=\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{1}\oplus\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{\widehat{e}}\,,

(5.127)

according to the braiding with the
D_{1}^{e}
line.
Then the symmetry category on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
is

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=\Sigma(\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{1})\,.

(5.128)

The club quiche furnishes a natural 2-functor

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\longrightarrow\Sigma(\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{1})\,,

(5.129)

whose image are the Wilson lines in
{\rm DW}(S_{3})_{(p-p^{\prime},t-t^{\prime})}
(all of which are in
\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{1}
) and their condensation defects.

(5.132)

Condensed Interface:

Consider the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
Condensed interface labeled by
H=Z_{3}

and

(5.134)

The F-symbols of the ends

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})\longrightarrow 2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})\,,\quad\mathcal{F}(D_{1}^{E})\cong D_{1}^{\omega}\oplus D_{1}^{\omega^{2}}\,,\quad\mathcal{F}(D_{1}^{P})\cong D_{1}^{\text{id}}\,.

(5.135)

5.6
Gapless Phases

Now we describe the theory obtained upon closing the club quiche by slotting in a physical boundary.
This will be referred to as a club sandwich.
This construction takes in an
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
symmetric quantum field theory and outputs an
\mathcal{S}
symmetric quantum field theory.
This construction has the merit as it can be used to realize transitions in systems with more complicated symmetry structures, using simpler ones.
This is a generalization of the Kennedy-Tasaki transformation that was originally formulated for
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetric quantum spin chains
[
84
]
.
It has subsequently been generalized to various contexts including for the study of transitions and gapless phases with fusion categorical symmetries
[
85
,
38
,
86
,
17
,
24
]
.
Here we use it for the study of transitions and gapless phases in theories with fusion 2-categorical symmetries.

5.6.1
KTs from
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
to
S_{3}

We now describe the KT transformations that takes a theory with
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form symmetry and outputs a theory with
S_{3}
0-form.
In the SymTFT picture we have

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}\,,

(5.136)

and we consider the quiches of section
5.5.1
.
There are two classes of interfaces between
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
and correspondingly two classes of KT transformations.

KT from the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
Condensed Interface.

Let us consider the club quiche corresponding to an
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[a]}
condensed interface, section
5.3.1
.
This produced a boundary

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\mathfrak{B}_{e}\,,

(5.137)

with symmetry
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
.
We may input a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form symmetric theory on the physical boundary.
The
S_{3}
symmetry is realized on this theory via the projection

2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}}\longrightarrow 2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\,.

(5.138)

In particular, the kernel of this projection is
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
for which, this theory realizes a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
SPT labeled by
p\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3},U(1))
.
Recall
p
was the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
projection of
\omega=(p,t)\in H^{3}(S_{3},U(1))
.
The data of
t\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
would modify the F-symbols of the ends of the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
surface on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
.
To summarize the
S_{3}
symmetry is realized as

KT from the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
Condensed Interface.

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
condensed interface, section
5.3.2
.
This produced a boundary

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{0}\ \oplus\ \left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{1}\ \oplus\ \left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{2}\,,

({\mathbb{Z}}_{3})
.

KT from the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
Condensed Interface.

Similarly, an
S_{3}
symmetric theory can be obtained from a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetric theory using a generalized KT transformation.
For this we consider the club quiche with
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
(carrying an
S_{3}
0-form symmetry) and the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
condensed interface such that the reduced TO is
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})
.
This club quiche produces a boundary condition for
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{0}\ \oplus\ \left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{1}\,,

(5.146)

where
\mathfrak{B}_{e}
is the Dirichlet boundary condition that carries a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
0-form symmetry.
The symmetry on this boundary is
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}={\rm Mat}_{2}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})
.
We now input a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
0-form symmetric theory on the physical boundary.
The
S_{3}
symmetry is realized on this theory via the projection

2\mathsf{Vec}_{S_{3}}\longrightarrow{\rm Mat}_{2}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})\,.

(5.147)

In particular, the Hilbert space of the theory obtained after compactifying the SymTFT decomposes into a direct sum of two
universes
corresponding to the two components of
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
.
The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form symmetry exchanges these universes/components while the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(0)}
symmetry acts within the components as (
5.78
)

S_{3}
symmetry is realized as

5.6.4
KTs from
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(0)}
to
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}

KT from the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
Condensed Interface.

Similarly, an
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetric theory can be obtained from a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
symmetric theory using a generalized KT transformation.
For this we consider the club quiche with
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}),p}
and the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
condensed interface such that the reduced TO is
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})
.
This club quiche produces a boundary condition for
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\left(\mathfrak{B}_{m}\right)_{0}\ \oplus\ \left(\mathfrak{B}_{m^{2}}\right)_{1}\,,

(5.155)

where
\mathfrak{B}_{m}
is the Neumann boundary condition that carries a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
1-form symmetry.
The symmetry on this boundary is
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}={\rm Mat}_{2}(2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}))
.
We now input a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
0-form symmetric theory
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}}
on the physical boundary.
The 2-group symmetry is realized on this theory via the 2-functor (see (
5.98
))

2\mathsf{Vec}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})\longrightarrow{\rm Mat}_{2}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}})\,.

(5.156)

In particular, the Hilbert space of the theory obtained after compactifying the SymTFT decomposes into a direct sum of two
universes
corresponding to the two components of
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
.
The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form symmetry exchanges these universes/components while the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}
symmetry acts within the components as (
5.78
)
To summarize the 2-group symmetry is realized as

(5.163)

KT from the

{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),t}
and the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
condensed interface such that the reduced TO is
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
.
This club quiche produces a boundary condition for
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\frac{\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{0}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}\ \boxplus\ \left(\frac{(\mathfrak{B}_{e})_{1}\ \boxplus\ (\mathfrak{B}_{e})_{2}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}\right)\,,

(5.164)

{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetric theory
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}

\frac{(\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})_{0}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}\ \boxplus\ \left(\frac{(\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})_{1}\ \boxplus\ (\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})_{2}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}\right)\,,

{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}

The Ising CFT has deformations to the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
broken and
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
preserving phases.
The
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
preserving phase (corresponding to the
\mathfrak{B}_{m}
boundary condition of the reduced TO),
produces a gapped phase

\frac{\rm Triv}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}\ \boxplus\ {\rm Triv}=\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})\ \boxplus\ \rm Triv\,,

(5.167)

where we have used
(\rm Triv\ \boxplus\ \rm Triv)/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\cong\rm Triv
.
This is the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
SSB phase (dubbed “superstar phase” in
[
2
]
) and has the interesting feature that one of its vacua is trivial (
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
preserving), while the other is topologically ordered (
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
breaking).
Conversely the deformation with the opposite flows to the symmetry broken phase, for which the underlying 3d TFT is
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}=\rm Triv\ \boxplus\ \rm Triv
, with the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetry exchanging the two components.
The
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
symmetric theory obtained by KT transforming this theory is

\left(\frac{\rm Triv\ \boxplus\ \rm Triv}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\right)\ \boxplus\ \left(\frac{\rm Triv\ \boxplus\ \rm Triv\ \boxplus\rm Triv\ \boxplus\ \rm Triv}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}\right)=\rm Triv\ \boxplus\ \rm Triv\ \boxplus Triv\,.

(5.168)

This gapped phase is very similar to a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
SSB phase, where the three vacua are cyclically permuted by the symmetry action, except that the non-invertible symmetry
D_{2}^{A}
acts as the direct sum of
{\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{a}
generators
D_{2}^{a}\oplus D_{2}^{a^{2}}
.
In this phase the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
form symmetry is trivial while the
D_{2}^{A}
non-invertible symmetry is spontaneously broken, therefore we refer to it as
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{3}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB Phase.

(5.179)

This is an
igSSB
for the 1-form symmetry, as it cannot be gapped without increasing the number of charged lines.
One way to see this is that for this gapless phase we have the lines
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[a]}
(see table
6
, with
H=S_{3}
and
N={\mathbb{Z}}_{3}
). For gapped phases, these get enhanced to either
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\oplus 2{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[a]}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{P}
or
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[a]}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[b]}
(see table 4 of
[
2
]
for the lines in the minimal gapped BC of DW(
S_{3}
)). So the number of
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
charged lines i.e. those arising from bulk surfaces ending on both
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
increase in the gapped phase. Thus we have an igSSB for the 1-form symmetry.

KT from the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
Condensed Interface.

Consider the club quiche with
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(S_{3}),(p,t)}
and the
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
condensed interface of section
5.3.2
such that the reduced TO is
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
.
This club quiche produces a boundary condition
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\mathfrak{B}_{m,t^{\prime}}
for
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
.
The symmetry category on this boundary is
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
and the
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
symmetry is implemented via a projection from
2\mathsf{Rep}(S_{3})
to
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
.
Then inserting a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
symmetric theory
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
on the physical boundary and compactifying the SymTFT produces the 3d theory

\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}/({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)},t-t^{\prime})\,.

6
Gapless Phases from
D_{8}
DW Theory

In this section we turn to symmetries that are realized as the fusion 2-categories of topological defects on gapped boundary conditions of the (3+1)d
D_{8}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory. Such gapped boundary conditions and gapped phases were discussed in
[
2
]
.
After a brief review of the
D_{8}
(3+1)d gauge theory, we discuss gapless (2+1)d phases with symmetries obtainable from
D_{8}
0-form symmetry via generalized gaugings.

6.1
The SymTFT

We present the group
D_{8}
(of symmetries of a square, sometimes referred to as
D_{4}
) as

D_{8}={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}=\big\langle r\,,\;x\ \big|\ r^{4}=x^{2}=\text{id}\,,\;xrx=r^{3}\big\rangle\,.

(6.1)

The
D_{8}
conjugacy classes are

[\text{id}]\,,\quad[r^{2}]\,,\quad[r]=\{r,\,r^{3}\}\,,\quad[x]=\{x,\,xr^{2}\}\,,\quad[xr]=\{xr,\,xr^{3}\}\,,

(6.2)

each of which labels a topological non-condensation surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}
:

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}\,,\quad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}\,.

(6.3)

Topological lines on each SymTFT surface are labeled by irreducible representations of the centralizer
H_{g}=\{h\in D_{8}\;|\;hg=gh\}
for
g
a representative of
[g]
, and are
[
2
]
:

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}:

\displaystyle\text{1End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R};\ R=1,1_{r},1_{x},1_{xr},E\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})

(6.4)

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}:

\displaystyle\text{1End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[r^{2}],R};\ R=1,1_{r},1_{x},1_{xr},E\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}:

\displaystyle\text{1End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[xr],R};\ R=(\epsilon_{1},\epsilon_{2}),\;\epsilon_{i}=\pm\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}:

\displaystyle\text{1End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[x],R};\ R=(\epsilon_{1},\epsilon_{2}),\;\epsilon_{i}=\pm\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

\displaystyle{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}:

\displaystyle\text{1End}({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]})=\left\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[r],R};\ R=1,i,-1,-i\right\}\cong\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})\,.

In particular, the topological lines on the identity surface (and thus genuine bulk topological lines),
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{[\text{id}],R}\equiv{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
, are labeled by
R\in\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
: we denote by
1_{k}
for
k\in\{r,x,xr\}
a 1-dimensional irrep that is 1 on
[1],[r^{2}],[k]
and
-1
otherwise, whereas for the 2-dimensional
E
we chose the following matrix representation:

\mathcal{D}_{E}(r)=\begin{pmatrix}i&0\\
0&-i\end{pmatrix}\,,\qquad\mathcal{D}_{E}(x)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\
1&0\end{pmatrix}\,.

(6.5)

6.2
Symmetries and Gapped Boundary Conditions

The topological boundary conditions of the (3+1)d
D_{8}
SymTFT were studied in detail in
[
2
]
and are summarized in table
7
. A convenient way to obtain any minimal boundary condition is to start with the Dirichlet boundary condition
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, which gives rise to
D_{8}
0-form symmetry
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
, and gauge a sub-group
H
of
D_{8}
. There is an additional choice of discrete torsion
\omega\in H^{3}(H,U(1))
in gauging
H
, which can be understood as stacking an
H
-SPT before gauging. The boundary condition obtained by gauging
H
with discrete torsion
\omega
is the
H
-Neumann boundary condition denoted as

\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(H),\omega}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}}{(H,\omega)}\,.

(6.6)

The non-invertible symmetry web for
D_{8}
, which includes (anomalous) 2-groups and 2-representation categories of 2-groups, was described in
[
46
]
and the SymTFT derivation provided in
[
2
]
. Here we will briefly summarize some specific cases.

\displaystyle\begin{array}[]{|c|c|c|l|}\hline\cr H=N&H^{3}(H,U(1))&H^{\text{diag}}&{\bm{Q}}_{p}\text{ that can end on }\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}(H),\omega}\\

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{r}}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}}\oplus 2{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\end{cases}\\

\hline\cr{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}&{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}&\langle(x,1)\rangle&\hskip-5.69054pt\begin{cases}{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}\\
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{x,1_{++}}\oplus 2{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{x,1_{+-}}\end{cases}\\
\hline\cr{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}&{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}&\langle(xr,1)\rangle&\hskip-5.69054pt\begin{cases}{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}\\
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{xr,1_{++}}\oplus 2{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{xr,1_{+-}}\end{cases}\\
\hline\cr D_{8}&{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}&\langle(r,1),\;(x,1)\rangle&\hskip-5.69054pt\begin{cases}{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[\text{id}]}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}\\

6.2.1
Dirichlet Boundary Condition

Each SymTFT line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
for
R\in\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
has
\text{dim}(R)
ends on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
which we denote as
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R,i}
with
i=1,\dots,\text{dim}(R)
.
We denote this as

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}\Bigg|_{\text{Dir}}=\left\{\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R,i}\ \Big|\ i=1,\dots,\text{dim}(R)\right\}\,.

(6.7)

Each bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}
splits into a direct sum of surfaces
D_{2}^{g}
for
g\in[g]
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, which fuse according to the group multiplication in
D_{8}
.
These are the generators of the
D_{8}
0-form symmetry on this boundary.
More specifically, the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}
has twisted sector ends
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{g}
for all
g\in[g]
, where the line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{g}
is in the twisted sector of the
D_{2}^{g}
defect on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
We denote this as

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}\Bigg|_{\text{Dir}}=\left\{(D_{2}^{g}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{g})\quad\Big|\quad g\in[g]\ \right\}\,.

(6.8)

The topological operators
\{\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R,i}\}
transform as an
R
-multiplet under the
D_{8}
symmetry.
We summarize the
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
boundary condition as (only the bulk defects with untwisted ends are shown) the quiche:

6.2.2
Neumann
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
Boundary Condition

This boundary conditions is obtained by gauging the non-normal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
with discrete torsion
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
.
The resulting boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),\omega}
has a 1-form symmetry whose generator we denote by
D_{1}^{1_{r}}
, an invertible 0-form symmetry generated by
D_{2}^{r^{2}}
and a non-invertible 0-form symmetry generated by a surface we will denote by
D_{2}^{[r]}
, which on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
was the composite object
D_{2}^{r}\oplus D_{2}^{r^{3}}
, constituting an orbit under
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
. It obeys the fusion
[
46
]
:

D_{2}^{[r]}\otimes D_{2}^{[r]}=\frac{D_{2}^{\text{id}}}{D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{1_{r}}}\oplus\frac{D_{2}^{r^{2}}}{D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{1_{r}}}\,.

(6.10)

Let us summarize the topological defects on this boundary, following
[
2
]
. Since the genuine local operator
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{1_{x}}
at the end of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}
was untwisted and uncharged under the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
symmetry, it remains unaltered after gauging and ends on this boundary.

The ends
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}
of
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, can be decomposed into linear combinations
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,\pm}=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,1}\pm\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,2}

with
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}
and
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}
respectively uncharged and charged under
D_{2}^{x}
.
Therefore, upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
, one obtains

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}\Bigg|_{{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}),\omega}}=(\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,+}\,,(D_{1}^{1_{r}}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{E,-}))\,.

(6.11)

The surfaces
D_{2}^{r}
and
D_{2}^{r^{3}}
are mapped to one another upon conjugation by
D_{2}^{x}
, therefore

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),\omega}=\left\{(D_{2}^{[r]}\,,\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[r]})\right\}\,,

(6.12)

where
D_{2}^{[r]}
is an indecomposable defect on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),\omega}
obeying the fusion (
6.10
).

The bulk SymTFT surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
can now end on this boundary, and gives rise to a line line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{x}
charged under
D_{1}^{1_{r}}
and with F-symbols given by
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,,U(1))
.
In summary, this boundary carries a symmetry corresponding to the 2-representations of the 2-group generated by a (non-condensation) non-invertible 0-form symmetry generator
D_{2}^{[r]}
, an invertible
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form symmetry generator
D_{2}^{r^{2}}
and a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form generator
D_{1}^{1_{r}}
.
This
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}),\omega}
boundary condition is depicted as the quiche
25
25

25

(6.13)

6.2.3
Neumann
D_{8}
Boundary Conditions

This boundary condition is obtained by gauging the full
D_{8}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
The SymTFT lines
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}
end on twisted sector local operators

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{R}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}(D_{8}),\omega}=(D_{1}^{R}\,,\mathcal{E}_{0}^{R})\,,

(6.14)

where the
D_{1}^{R}
generate a
\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
1-form symmetry and are:

D_{1}^{1}\,,\quad D_{1}^{1_{x}}\,,\quad D_{1}^{1_{r}}\,,\quad D_{1}^{1_{xr}}\,,\quad D_{1}^{E}\,,

(6.15)

whose fusions follow from the tensor products of irreps (for
1_{k}=1_{x}\,,\;1_{r}\,,\;1_{xr}
):

\displaystyle D_{1}^{1_{x}}\otimes D_{1}^{1_{r}}

\displaystyle=D_{1}^{1_{xr}}\,,\quad D_{1}^{1_{k}}\otimes D_{1}^{1_{k}}=D_{1}^{1}\,,

(6.16)

\displaystyle D_{1}^{E}\otimes D_{1}^{E}

\displaystyle=D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{1_{x}}\oplus D_{1}^{1_{r}}\oplus D_{1}^{1_{xr}}\,.

The 1-dimensional irreps thus generate an invertible
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
1-form symmetry, whereas
D_{1}^{E}
is non-invertible.
The SymTFT surfaces end on single untwisted sector lines

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[g]}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}(D_{8}),\omega}=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[g]}\,.

(6.17)

The line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[g]}
has a braiding phase of
\chi_{R}([g])
with
D_{1}^{R}
.
The lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[g]}
have F-symbols that are determined by
\omega\in H^{3}(D_{8},U(1))
and are those of the 3d
D_{8}
Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with topological action
\omega

[
81
]
.
All other symmetry defects on this boundary can be obtained as condensation defects constructed from the
\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})
lines.
The boundary condition can be summarized as (only the bulk defects with untwisted ends are shown)

6.3
Minimal Interfaces

We now turn to the minimal interfaces from the
D_{8}
TO to a reduced TO. These are given in terms of the usual data

(H,N,\pi,\omega)
, specifying an interface between
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
. We have listed these in table
8
. We note that if
N=1
, then
H=H/N
so one must choose trivial twist
\pi\in H^{4}(H/N,U(1))
for it to be trivial when pulled-back to
H
. Instead, for
H=D_{8}
and
N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
, we can pick a non-trivial
\pi\in H^{4}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
, as we will discuss below.

H=D_{8}
and
N=1
, describes the transparent interface within
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}})
. Let us therefore analyze the other possibilities, corresponding to interfaces between
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
, which will then give rise to gapless phases upon fixing
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
boundary conditions.

6.3.1
Interface to
\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})

There is a single class of minimal interface between
{\rm DW}(D_{8})
and
{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})
.
We denote the topological defects of
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})
as:

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e^{p}}\,,\qquad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m^{p}}\,,\qquad p\in\{0,1,2,3\}\,.

(6.19)

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{r}}
Condensed Interface.

This class of interfaces is characterized by
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}\,,\;N=1
. Since
N
is trivial, no (non-identity) surfaces can end on this interface.
For the topological lines, we consider the projection:

\displaystyle\kappa:

\displaystyle\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})

\displaystyle\to\qquad\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})

(6.20)

\displaystyle(D_{1}^{1_{r}},\,D_{1}^{1_{x}},\,D_{1}^{1_{xr}},\,D_{1}^{E})

\displaystyle\mapsto(D_{1}^{1},\,D_{1}^{e^{2}},\,D_{1}^{e^{2}},\,D_{1}^{e}\oplus D_{1}^{e^{3}})

implying that the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{r}}
can end on this interface. The deconfined surfaces are labeled by
[g]
for
g\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}
, in particular,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}
splits on this interface into
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{r}\oplus{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{r^{3}}
. The group
H^{\text{diag}}
(see table
8
), describes the mapping of topological surfaces:
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{r^{p}}
becomes
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m^{p}}
in
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4})
.

(6.21)

There is also a choice of
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
that translates to the associators of the lines obtained from bulk surfaces intersecting the interface.

6.3.2
Interfaces to
\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

Let us now discuss the classes of interfaces to
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
, whose topological defects we denote as:

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e_{1}^{p}e_{2}^{q}}\,,\qquad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m_{1}^{p}m_{2}^{q}}\,,\qquad p,q\in\{0,1\}\,.

(6.22)

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}
Condensed Interface.

This class of interfaces is obtained by setting
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\,,\;N=1
. Since
N
is trivial, no (non-identity) surfaces can end on this interface.
For the topological lines, we consider the projection:

\displaystyle\kappa:

\displaystyle\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})

\displaystyle\to\qquad\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

(6.23)

\displaystyle(D_{1}^{1_{r}},\,D_{1}^{1_{x}},\,D_{1}^{1_{xr}},\,D_{1}^{E})

\displaystyle\mapsto(D_{1}^{e_{2}},\,D_{1}^{1},\,D_{1}^{e_{2}},\,D_{1}^{e_{1}}\oplus D_{1}^{e_{1}e_{2}})

implying that the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}
is condensed on this interface. The deconfined surfaces are labeled by
g\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
, in particular,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
splits on this interface into

(6.24)

The choice of
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{3}
translates to the associators of the lines obtained from bulk surfaces intersecting the interface.

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}}
Condensed Interface.

This is obtained by setting
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}\,,\;N=1
. Its properties are very similar to the previous case, and can be determined from it by performing the automorphism relating the following equivalent presentations of
D_{8}
:

\displaystyle D_{8}=\mathbb{Z}_{4}^{r}\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{x}:

\displaystyle\{\text{id},\,r,\,r^{2},\,r^{3},x,xr,xr^{2},xr^{3}\}\,,

(6.25)

\displaystyle D_{8}=\mathbb{Z}_{4}^{r}\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_{2}^{xr}:

\displaystyle\{\text{id},\,r,\,r^{2},\,r^{3},xr,xr^{2},xr^{3},x\}\,.

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
Condensed Interface.

By setting
H=D_{8}\,,\;N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
the surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
can end on the interface since
N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
, while no (non-identity) topological lines can end since
H=D_{8}
.
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
is confined since it braids non-trivially with the condensed
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
.
The deconfined surfaces are labeled by
g\in D_{8}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}\simeq{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
and the group
H^{\text{diag}}
(see table
8
), describes the mapping of topological surfaces. For
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
there is a possible non-trivial 4-cocycle twist
\pi\in H^{4}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
, which trivializes when pulled-back to
D_{8}
, to which we will return in section
6.4
. The map of generalized charges is:

(6.26)

The choice of
\omega\in H^{3}(D_{8},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
translates to the associators of the lines obtained from bulk surfaces intersecting the interface.

6.3.3
Interfaces to
\rm DW({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

Let us now turn to the interfaces between
{\rm DW}(D_{8})
and
{\rm DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
, whose topological defects we denote as:

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{e^{p}}\,,\qquad{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m^{p}}\,,\qquad p\in\{0,1\}\,.

(6.27)

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{r}},{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}},{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}}
Condensed Interface.

This is obtained by choosing
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}\,,\;N=1
. Since
N
is trivial, no (non-identity) surfaces can end on this interface.
For the topological lines, we consider the projection:

\displaystyle\kappa:

\displaystyle\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})

\displaystyle\to\quad\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

(6.28)

\displaystyle(D_{1}^{1_{k}},\,D_{1}^{E})

\displaystyle\mapsto(D_{1}^{1},\,2D_{1}^{e})\,,\qquad k\in\{r,x,xr\}\,,

implying that the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{k}}
for all 1-dim irreps can end on this interface. The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
is deconfined and becomes the magnetic surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
:

(6.29)

There is also a choice of
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
that translates to the associators of the line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[r^{2}]m}
obtained from the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
intersecting the interface.

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}},{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{E}}
Condensed Interface.

This is obtained by choosing
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\,,\;N=1
. Since
N
is trivial, no (non-identity) surfaces can end on this interface. For the topological lines, we consider the projection:

\displaystyle\kappa:

\displaystyle\mathsf{Rep}(D_{8})

\displaystyle\to\qquad\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})

(6.30)

\displaystyle(D_{1}^{1_{r}},\,D_{1}^{1_{x}},\,D_{1}^{1_{xr}},\,D_{1}^{E})

\displaystyle\mapsto(D_{1}^{e},\,D_{1}^{1},\,D_{1}^{e},\,D_{1}^{1}\oplus D_{1}^{e})

implying that the lines
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
can end on this interface. The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
is deconfined and becomes the magnetic surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
:

(6.31)

There is also a choice of
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
that translates to the associators of the line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{[x]m}
obtained from the bulk surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
intersecting the interface.

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}},{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{E}}
Condensed Interface.

This is obtained by setting
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{xr}
and
N=1
. Its properties are very similar to the previous case, and can be determined from it by using the automorphism relating the two presentations of
D_{8}
in equation (
6.25
).

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}},{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
Condensed Interface.

Setting

) (since it depends only on

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}
can end on this interface. The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
is deconfined and becomes the magnetic surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}

(6.32)

There is also a choice of
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,U(1))
that translates to the associators of the lines obtained from the bulk surfaces intersecting the interface.

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}},{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
Condensed Interface.

Its properties are very similar to the previous case, and can be determined from it by using the automorphism relating the two presentations of
D_{8}
in equation (
6.25
).

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}},{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
Condensed Interface.

H={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}\,,\;N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
can end on the interface. For the topological lines, we consider the same projection as (
6.23
) (since it depends only on

), implying that the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}
can end on this interface. The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
is deconfined and becomes the magnetic surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
:

(6.33)

There is also a choice of
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\,U(1))
that translates to the associators of the lines obtained from the bulk surfaces intersecting the interface.

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}},{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[xr]}
Condensed Interface.

Its properties are very similar to the previous case, and can be determined from it by using the automorphism relating the two presentations of
D_{8}
in equation (
6.25
).

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{r}},{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
Condensed Interface.

Setting
H={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}\,,\;N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
, the topological surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
can end on the interface. For the topological lines, we consider the same projection as (
6.20
) (since it depends only on
H
), implying that the line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{r}}
can end on this interface. The surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}
is deconfined and becomes the magnetic surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{m}
:

(6.34)

There is also a choice of
\omega\in H^{3}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
that translates to the associators of the lines obtained from the bulk surfaces intersecting the interface.

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
Condensed Interface.

By setting
H=D_{8}\,,\;N={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{r}
the surfaces
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
can end on the interface, while no (non-identity) topological lines can end since
H=D_{8}
.
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
is confined since it braids non-trivially with the condensed
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
, and so are
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{x}}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}}
since they braid with
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r]}
.

(6.35)

There is also a choice of
\omega\in H^{3}(D_{8},U(1))
that translates to the associators of the lines obtained from the bulk surfaces intersecting the interface.

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
Condensed Interface.

By setting
H=D_{8}\,,\;N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
the surfaces
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
can end on the interface, while no (non-identity) topological lines can end since
H=D_{8}
.
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{E}
is confined since it braids non-trivially with the condensed
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
, and so are
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{r}}
and
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{1_{xr}}
since they braid with
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
.

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
Condensed Interface.

).

6.4
Gapless Phases

We can now consider the club sandwiches, obtained by inserting various
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
on the club quiches from the last section, and choosing specific gapless phases (for a symmetry realized by the reduced TO) as
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
. We will highlight some interesting phases, such as igSPTs and igSSBs.

6.4.1
igSPT for
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}

By setting
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, we fix the symmetry to be
2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}
, i.e.
D_{8}
0-form symmetry, as reviewed in section
6.2.1
.

If we fix
G=H=D_{8}
and
N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}
, the reduced topological order
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
can have a non-trivial 4-cocycle twist
\pi\in H^{4}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
. To construct a representative of
\pi
whose pullback to
D_{8}
is trivial, we follow the approach described on page
2.3
, by writing
\pi=\eta\cup e
, for
\eta\in H^{2}(H/N,\widehat{N})
and
e\in H^{2}(H/N,N)
. We choose
\eta\in H^{2}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{m_{1}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{m_{2}},{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{\widehat{r}^{2}})
to be:

\eta(m_{1}^{p_{1}}m_{2}^{p_{2}},\,m_{1}^{q_{1}}m_{2}^{q_{2}}\,|\,\widehat{r}^{2})=(-1)^{p_{2}q_{1}}\,,

(6.37)

and
+1
otherwise. For the section
s:{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\to D_{8}
, we pick:

s(m_{1})=x\,,\quad s(m_{2})=r\,,\quad s(m_{1}m_{2})=xr^{3}\,,

(6.38)

with representative
e\in H^{2}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{m_{1}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{m_{2}},{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}})
of the extension class given by equation (
2.33
), whose non-trivial values are:

\begin{split}e(m_{1},m_{2})=r^{2}\,,\qquad e(m_{1},m_{1}m_{2})=r^{2}\,,\cr e(m_{2},m_{2})=r^{2}\,,\qquad e(m_{2},m_{1}m_{2})=r^{2}\,.\end{split}

(6.39)

Therefore
\pi=\eta\cup e\in H^{4}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{m_{1}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{m_{2}},U(1))
is given by:

\pi(m_{1}^{a_{1}}m_{2}^{a_{2}},m_{1}^{b_{1}}m_{2}^{b_{2}},m_{1}^{c_{1}}m_{2}^{c_{2}},m_{1}^{d_{1}}m_{2}^{d_{2}})=(-1)^{a_{2}b_{1}c_{1}d_{2}+a_{2}b_{1}c_{2}d_{2}}

(6.40)

which we checked to be a representative of a non-trivial cohomology class in
H^{4}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2},U(1))
.

Club Quiche from
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
Condensed Interface.

Let us consider the club quiche corresponding to the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
condensed interface, see (
6.26
).
This produces a boundary

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\mathfrak{B}_{e_{1},e_{2}}\,,

(6.41)

with symmetry
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}^{\pi}
. We may input a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form symmetric theory with anomaly
\pi\in H^{4}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
, denoted by
\mathfrak{T}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}^{\pi}
, on the physical boundary.
The
D_{8}
symmetry is realized on this theory via the projection

\displaystyle 2\mathsf{Vec}_{D_{8}}

\displaystyle\longrightarrow 2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}^{\pi}\,,

(6.42)

\displaystyle(D_{2}^{r^{2p}},\,D_{2}^{xr^{2p}},\,D_{2}^{r^{2p+1}},\,D_{2}^{xr^{2p+1}})

\displaystyle\longmapsto(D_{2}^{\text{id}},\,D_{2}^{m_{1}},\,D_{2}^{m_{2}},\,D_{2}^{m_{1}m_{2}})\,,\qquad p\in\{0,1\}

whose kernel is
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}
and the
D_{8}
0-form symmetry is realized as

The gapless phase resulting from
\mathcal{I}_{(D_{8},{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}},\pi,\omega)}
preserves the full
D_{8}
. For non-trivial
\pi
, equation (
6.40
), it is intrinsically gapless since if we gap the theory,
D_{8}
must get spontaneously broken to a subgroup
H^{\prime}<D_{8}
such that
\pi|_{H^{\prime}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}}}=1
. From table
8
we see that this holds for all proper subgroups
H^{\prime}<D_{8}
so this phase can be gapped to all
D_{8}
gapped phases in which
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[r^{2}]}
is condensed (since it was already condensed on
\mathcal{I}_{(D_{8},{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{r^{2}},\pi,\omega)}
), except for the
D_{8}
SPTs. This is shown in figure
7
, where, for simplicity, we have set all 3-cocycles to the identity.
It would be interesting to determine the input transitions for these igSPTs, which are
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
symmetric gapless phases, with specific 4-cocycles.

6.4.2
D_{8}
-symmetric Phase Transitions

These can be computed analogously to the
S_{3}
example of section
5
. Table
1
summarizes the results for transitions between two
D_{8}
gapped phases: these are obtained from
D_{8}
club quiches with reduced TO
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}})
, by performing a KT transformation taking the input CFT to be 3d Ising. If the resulting gapless has a single copy of Ising it is a gSPT, otherwise it is gSSB for
D_{8}
0-form symmetry. Each gapless universe preserves a subgroup of
D_{8}
ismororphic to
H
while the universes are permuted by representatives of the other
H
-cosets of
D_{8}
. gSPTs thus correspond to phases for which
H=D_{8}
.

6.4.3
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)})
-symmetric Phase Transitions

By setting
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x})}
, we fix the symmetry to be
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{G}})
where
{\mathbb{G}}={\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{(1)}\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}
, i.e. a 2-representation of 2-group symmetry that can be obtained from
D_{8}
0-form symmetry by gauging the non normal
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
, as reviewed in section
6.2.2
.

We can thus determine the gapless phases corresponding to transitions between two
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{G}})
-symmetric gapped phases by gauging the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
symmetry of the
D_{8}
CFTs of table
1
. If
N={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
, after gauging we get a
\text{DW}({\mathbb{Z}}_{2})
stacking: its charged line comes from the bulk
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{[x]}
ending on both
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{phys}}
. If
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
is a subset of
H
but not of
N
, we have to gauge the
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}
0-form symmetry of 3d
\mathsf{Ising}
: the resulting
\frac{\mathsf{Ising}}{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(0)}}
theory realizes a transition between
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
trivial and
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{(1)}
SSB phases. If, finally,
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
is not a subgroup of
H
, then we have to combine the gapless universes into
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
orbits: upon gauging
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
we obtain a single
\mathsf{Ising}
from each pair that forms a
{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}^{x}
