Appendix A
Partial Ordering on Minimal
Interfaces

This partial ordering can be seen from the corresponding condensable algebras
[
32
]
, where the condensable algebra associated to the interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
is the
G
-crossed braided multifusion category

\text{Fun}_{H}(G,\mathsf{Vec}_{N}^{\omega|_{N}})\,,

(A.1)

with the crossed braided structure determined by
\omega
and
\pi

26
26

26

There is a technical subtlety that we suppressed in the main text, being the monoidal functor specifying the
H
action
\rho:H\rightarrow\text{Aut}^{\text{br}}(\mathsf{Vec})
on the trivially graded component of
\mathsf{Vec}_{N}^{\omega|_{N}}
, and technically we also require
H_{1}
and
H_{2}
to have compatible actions for the partial ordering to hold true, i.e.,
\rho_{i}:H_{i}\rightarrow\text{Aut}^{\text{br}}(\mathsf{Vec})
for
i=1,2
are such that

\rho_{2}=\rho_{1}\circ\iota,

(A.2)

where
\iota:H_{2}\hookrightarrow H_{1}
.
.
The desired partial orderings takes two steps

\mathcal{I}_{(H_{1},N_{1},\pi_{1},\omega_{1},)}<\mathcal{I}_{(H_{2},N_{1},\widetilde{\pi},\omega_{2})}<\mathcal{I}_{(H_{2},N_{2},\pi_{2},\omega_{2})},

(A.3)

for suitable
\widetilde{\pi}\in H^{4}(H_{2}/N_{1},U(1))
, which will be explicit in the following. For the partial ordering to hold true, the
G
-crossed braided structure on the condensable algebras should be compatible. In the first step, this is guaranteed by the requirement that
\omega_{2}=\omega_{1}|_{H_{2}}
and
\widetilde{\pi}=\pi_{1}|_{H_{2}/N_{1}}
27
27

27

The compatible
H_{i}
action
\rho_{2}=\rho_{1}\circ\iota
also plays a role here.
, under which there is the inclusion

\begin{split}\text{Fun}_{H_{1}}(G,\mathsf{Vec}_{N_{1}}^{\omega_{1}|_{N_{1}}})&\hookrightarrow\text{Fun}_{H_{2}}(G,\mathsf{Vec}_{N_{1}}^{\omega_{2}|_{N_{1}}})\\
F&\mapsto F\,.\end{split}

(A.4)

Similarly, for the condensable algebra associated to
\mathcal{I}_{(H_{2},N_{1},\widetilde{\pi},\omega_{2})}
to be a subalgebra of that associated to
\mathcal{I}_{(H_{2},N_{2},\pi_{2},\omega_{2})}
, the requirement
\widetilde{\pi}=p^{*}\pi_{2}
guarantees the natural inclusion

\begin{split}\text{Fun}_{H_{2}}(G,\mathsf{Vec}_{N_{1}}^{\omega_{2}|_{N_{1}}})&\hookrightarrow\text{Fun}_{H_{2}}(G,\mathsf{Vec}_{N_{2}}^{\omega_{2}|_{N_{2}}})\\
F&\mapsto F\,.\end{split}

(A.5)

Appendix B
Gapless Phases from Abelian DW Theories

In this section, we study phase transitions for symmetries that arise as gapped boundary conditions of DW theories for an abelian group
{\mathbb{A}}
and trivial topological action in
H^{4}({\mathbb{A}},U(1))
. The minimal symmetries are generically 2-groups with mixed anomalies, and the non-minimal cases are obtained by stacking the Dirichlet BC with an
{\mathbb{A}}
-symmetric TQFT and gauging a subgroup
{\mathbb{B}}<{\mathbb{A}}
.
The gapped BCs and gapped phases were completely classified in
[
1
]
. Here we will extend this analysis to gapless phases and phase-transitions in the presence of such symmetries.

B.1
The SymTFT

Let
{\mathbb{A}}
be a finite abelian group, and let us consider the SymTFT for the 0-form symmetry
{\mathbb{A}}
. Its topological defects are given in terms of the Drinfeld center
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}})
, whose non-condensation defects are

\{{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{a}\,,\quad a\in{\mathbb{A}}\}\quad\text{and}\quad\{{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\hat{a}}\,,\quad\widehat{a}\in\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}}\}\,.

(B.1)

where
\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}}=\text{Hom}({\mathbb{A}},U(1))
denotes the Pontryagin dual (or the group of multiplicative characters) of the abelian group
{\mathbb{A}}
. We have simplified our general notation
The surface and line defects braid with

B({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{a},{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}})=\widehat{a}(a).

(B.2)

Summary of minimal gapped BC for
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}})
. Here
\nu
denotes the discrete torsion,
{\mathbb{B}}<{\mathbb{A}}
is a subgroup,
\beta
is defined by equation (
B.15
),
\widehat{a}\in\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}}}
is identified with
\widehat{a}\in\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}}
such that
\widehat{a}|_{{\mathbb{B}}}=1
, and
\mathbb{G}^{(2)}=({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)}
is a two-group.

Dirichlet
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.

The topological defects that can end on the Dirichlet boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
are the identity surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{\text{id}}
, and all the topological lines
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}
, labeled by
\widehat{a}\in\widehat{A}
.
The Dirichlet BC realizes the symmetry
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}}
, with symmetry generators
D_{2}^{a}
,
a\in{\mathbb{A}}
.
Specifically, on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, the bulk surface operator
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{a}
ends on a line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a}
attached to the
D_{2}^{a}
symmetry defect.
We denote this as

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{a}\Bigg|_{\text{Dir}}=(D_{2}^{a},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{1})\,.

(B.3)

Similarly, the bulk line
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}
ends on an untwisted local operator

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}\Bigg|_{\text{Dir}}=\mathcal{E}_{0}^{\widehat{a}}\,,

(B.4)

which are charged under the symmetry
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}}
due to the bulk braiding (
B.2
)

B(D_{2}^{a},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{\widehat{a}})=B({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{a},{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}})=\widehat{a}(a).

(B.5)

Neumann with
\nu
.

The Neumann boundary condition
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu},\nu}
is obtained by gauging the
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}}
symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
with the discrete torsion
\nu\in H^{3}({\mathbb{A}},U(1))
.
The line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a}
, in the twisted sector of
D_{2}^{a}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
is gauged to the untwisted sector, hence all the defect surface
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{a}
for
a\in{\mathbb{A}}
, can end on non-genuine lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu},\nu}
,

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{a}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu},\nu}=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a}\,.

(B.6)

Note that these lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a}
are not unique, in fact there are
|{\mathbb{A}}|
lines from fusing with the end of
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{\text{id}}
, which are genuine lines that form
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})
.
These non-genuine lines have
F
-symbols determined by the discrete torsion

F(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a_{1}},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a_{2}},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a_{3}})=\nu(a_{1},a_{2},a_{3})\,.

(B.7)

On the other hand, the charged operators
\mathcal{E}_{0}^{\widehat{a}}
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
,
\widehat{a}\in\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}}
, are gauged into twisted sectors hence the lines
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}
do not end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu},\nu}

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu},\nu}=(D_{1}^{\widehat{a}},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{\widehat{a}})\,,

(B.8)

to form the generators
D_{1}^{\widehat{a}}
of the symmetry
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu},\nu}
.
The non-genuine lines are charged non-trivially under the symmetry
\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})
due to the bulk braiding (
B.2
)

B(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a},D_{1}^{\widehat{a}})=B({\bm{Q}}_{2}^{a},{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}})=\widehat{a}(a)\,.

(B.9)

Partial Neumann
(\mathbb{B},\nu)
.

The partial Neumann boundary condition
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{B}}),\nu}
is obtained by gauging a subgroup
{\mathbb{B}}<{\mathbb{A}}
symmetry with a discrete torsion
\nu\in H^{3}({\mathbb{B}},U(1))
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
After gauging
{\mathbb{B}}<{\mathbb{A}}
, a surface defect
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{b}
labeled by
b\in{\mathbb{B}}
can end on a non-genuine line
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}
on the boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{B}}),\nu}

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{b}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{B}}),\nu}=\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b}\,.

(B.10)

The
F
-symbols for these lines are determined by
\nu

F(\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b_{1}},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b_{2}},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{b_{3}})=\nu(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3})\,.

(B.11)

After this gauging, there is still a residual
{\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}}
0-form symmetry.
Bulk lines
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}
which are uncharged under
{\mathbb{B}}
, i.e., those that satisfy

\widehat{a}\Big|_{{\mathbb{B}}}=1\,,

(B.12)

continue to end on local untwisted topological operators on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{B}}),\nu}
. The remaining lines generate a dual
\widehat{{\mathbb{B}}}\cong{\mathbb{B}}
1-form symmetry.
Specifically the following two short exact sequences are useful

\begin{split}&1\longrightarrow{\mathbb{B}}\longrightarrow{\mathbb{A}}\overset{\phi}{\longrightarrow}{\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}}\longrightarrow 1\,,\\
&1\longrightarrow\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}}}\longrightarrow\widehat{\mathbb{A}}\overset{\widehat{\phi}}{\longrightarrow}\widehat{\mathbb{B}}\longrightarrow 1\,.\end{split}

(B.13)

The boundary projections of the bulk SymTFT defects are given in terms of the projection maps
\phi
and
\widehat{\phi}
as

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{a}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{B}}),\nu}=(D_{2}^{\phi(a)},\mathcal{E}_{1}^{a})\,,\qquad{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}\Bigg|_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{B}}),\nu}=(D_{1}^{\widehat{\phi}(\widehat{a})},\mathcal{E}_{0}^{\widehat{a}})\,,

(B.14)

Let the extension class of the first short exact sequence in (
B.13
) be denoted as
\epsilon\in H^{2}({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}},{\mathbb{B}})
.
There is a possibly non-trivial mixed anomaly
\beta\in H^{4}\left(({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)},U(1)\right)
between the 1-form
{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)}=\widehat{{\mathbb{B}}}
and the 0-form
({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}
symmetry, described by the topological action
[
88
]

\int_{M_{4}}B_{2}\cup\epsilon(A_{1})\in{\mathbb{R}}/2\pi{\mathbb{Z}}\,,

(B.15)

where
\epsilon\in H^{2}({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}},{\mathbb{B}})
denotes the extension class

1\rightarrow{\mathbb{B}}\rightarrow{\mathbb{A}}\rightarrow{\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}}\rightarrow 1\,,

(B.16)

B_{2}\in H^{2}(M_{4},\widehat{{\mathbb{B}}})
and
A_{1}\in H^{1}(M_{4},{\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})
are the background gauge fields for the 1-form and 0-form symmetries respectively.
We denote the symmetry on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{B}}),\nu}
by

2\mathsf{Vec}^{\beta}({({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)}})\,.

(B.17)

B.3
Minimal Interfaces

Following the general theory, the minimal interfaces

\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}\,,

(B.18)

where
N<H<{\mathbb{A}}
are subgroups,
\omega\in H^{3}(H,U(1))
and
\pi\in H^{4}(H/N,U(1))
such that

p^{*}\pi=0
, where
p:H\twoheadrightarrow H/N
.
The surfaces that end on the interface are
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{n}
for
n\in N
. Whereas the reduced TO, which depends on
\pi
, is

\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})\,.

(B.19)

The lines that can end on the interface are given by

\widehat{a}\in\widehat{\mathbb{A}/H}\,.

(B.20)

The cocycle
\omega
specifies the associator of the lines at the intersection where
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{h}
passes through
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
to become
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{p(h)}
.
We denote these lines as
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{h}
.
In the special case that
h\in N<H
,
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{h}
ends on the interface.

Interfaces from Folding.

We examine the construction of such interfaces from the folding and gauging process. Consider the Drinfeld center of the folded theory

\overline{\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}})}\boxtimes{\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})}\,,

(B.21)

and impose the Dirichlet boundary condition.
By appropriately gauging and unfolding, one can recover all the possible interfaces between
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
. In particular, gauging the diagonal subgroup
H^{\text{diag}}
on the Dirichlet boundary defined as

H\cong H^{\text{diag}}=\{(h,p(h))\,|\,h\in H\}\subset{\mathbb{A}}\times H/N,

(B.22)

(recall
p:H\twoheadrightarrow H/N
denotes the canonical projection) with a choice of discrete torsion
\omega\in H^{3}(H^{\text{diag}},U(1))
, gives rise (after unfolding) to the SymTFT interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\omega,\pi)}
between
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
.
The map from defects of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
to defects of
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}})
is

\begin{split}\mathcal{F}:\quad\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})&\rightarrow\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}})\\
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{hN}&\mapsto\bigoplus_{h^{\prime}\in hN}{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{h^{\prime}}\,,\\
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}^{\prime}}&\mapsto\bigoplus_{\widehat{a}\in\text{Ind}^{{\mathbb{A}}}_{H}p^{*}\widehat{a}^{\prime}}{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}\,,\end{split}

(B.23)

where
hN\in H/N
is a coset,
\widehat{a}^{\prime}\in\widehat{H/N}
and the direct sum over
\widehat{a}\in\text{Ind}^{{\mathbb{A}}}_{H}p^{*}\widehat{a}^{\prime}
is taken over all the representations of
{\mathbb{A}}
that appear in the decomposition of the induced representation, computed via

\text{Ind}^{{\mathbb{A}}}_{H}p^{*}\widehat{a}^{\prime}={\mathbb{C}}[{\mathbb{A}}]\otimes_{{\mathbb{C}}[H]}p^{*}\widehat{a}^{\prime}\,{,}

(B.24)

which is isomorphic to the direct sum of irreducible representations
\widehat{a}\in\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})
such that
\kappa(\widehat{a})\cong p^{*}\widehat{a}^{\prime}
where
\kappa:\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})\to\mathsf{Rep}(H)
is the forgetful functor.
Here
{\mathbb{C}}[G]
denotes the group algebra, being the regular representation of a finite group
G
, i.e.,
{\mathbb{C}}[G]\cong\bigoplus_{R}\text{dim}(R)R
, summed over all irreducible representations of
G
. Pictorially, we find

B.4
Minimal Club Quiches

Consider an interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
between
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}})
and
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
. By choosing different symmetry boundaries
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}
, we study the different symmetries
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
and boundary conditions
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
after compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}})
.

B.4.1
\mathbb{A}^{(0)}
0-Form Symmetry

Starting with the
\mathcal{S}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}}
0-form symmetry corresponding to the the symmetry boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{sym}}=\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
.
Recall the lines that can end on
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
form
\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/H}
, and all lines can end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\rm Dir}
. After compactifying the
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}})
SymTFT, the lines
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}
for
\widehat{a}\in\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/H}
become the local operators
\mathcal{O}^{\widehat{a}}
, with OPEs satisfying the group multiplication of
\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/H}
:

(B.26)

Note
\mathcal{O}^{\widehat{a}}
is charged under
D_{2}^{a}
if
a\not\in H
,
hence the symmetry
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}}
is broken to
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H}
.
Fix a set
X
of coset representatives for
{\mathbb{A}}/H
. From the above local operators, one can build
|{\mathbb{A}}/H|
idempotents
\Pi_{x}
labeled by
x\in X

28
28

28

Again, recall we view
\widehat{a}\in\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/H}
as the element
\widehat{a}\in\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}}
such that
\widehat{a}|_{H}=1
associated via the universal property of a quotient group.

\Pi_{x}=\frac{1}{|{\mathbb{A}}/H|}\sum_{\widehat{a}\in\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/H}}\widehat{a}(x)\mathcal{O}^{\widehat{a}}\,.

(B.27)

After taking the club quiche, the
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{n}
surface for
n\in N
gives lines in twisted sectors

(D_{2}^{n},\mathcal{L}^{n})\,

(B.28)

that satisfy the
N
fusion rule with associator
\omega|_{N}
.
The boundary after compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}})
is

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\bigoplus_{x\in X}\left(\mathfrak{B}_{e}\right)_{x}\,,

(B.29)

where
\mathfrak{B}_{e}
is the Dirichlet boundary condition of the
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})
SymTFT.
The 2-category of topological defects on this boundary form

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=\text{Mat}_{|X|}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})\,,

(B.30)

which is a multifusion 2-category whose objects are
|X|\times|X|
matrices with entries in
2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi}
.
We obtain the 2-functor between symmetry categories

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}}\rightarrow\text{Mat}_{|X|}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N}^{\pi})\,,

(B.31)

Under this functor,
D_{2}^{a}
acts on the components of
\mathcal{S}^{\prime}
via the natural
{\mathbb{A}}
action on
H
cosets in
{\mathbb{A}}
.
Specifically,
H<{\mathbb{A}}
leaves the components fixed.
In
H
, further,
N<H
acts trivially upto a modification of associators, representative of an
N
-SPT labeled by
\omega\in H^{3}(N,U(1))
.
Finally, the
H/N
symmetry is realized as a
H/N
symmetry on a given component
\mathfrak{B}_{e}
of the reduced TO.
Putting all this together, we obtain the functor

\mathcal{F}(D_{2}^{a})=\bigoplus_{x\in X}\left(D_{2}^{p(h)}\right)_{y,x}\,,

(B.32)

where
a=yhx^{-1}
for some unique
y\in X
and
h\in H
given
x\in X
,

\left(D_{2}^{p(h)}\right)_{y,x}=1_{y,x}\otimes\left(D_{2}^{p(h)}\right)_{x,x}=\left(D_{2}^{p(h)}\right)_{y,y}\otimes 1_{y,x}\,.

(B.33)

and
1_{y,x}
is the invertible surface that has the following linking action on the idempotents labeled by
x^{\prime}\in X

1_{y,x}\Pi_{x^{\prime}}=\delta_{x,x^{\prime}}\Pi_{y}\,.

(B.34)

B.4.2
1-Form Symmetry

By gauging with discrete torsion
\nu\in H^{3}({\mathbb{A}},U(1))
we get 1-form symmetry
\mathbb{A}^{(1)}
(or
2\mathsf{Rep}(\mathbb{A})
).
Lets consider the interfaces in this case:
The lines that can end on the interface
\mathcal{I}(H,N,\omega)
form
\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/H}<\widehat{\mathbb{A}}
.
None of the non-trivial lines can end on this boundary. The surfaces that can both end on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu},\nu}
and on the interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\omega)}
are
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{n}
for
n\in N
. They form line operators
\mathcal{L}^{n}
after compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}})

(B.35)

Therefore after compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}})
, these provide local operators attached to the generators of the 1-form symmetry subgroup
\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/H}
, which is trivialized.
The 1-form symmetry that acts faithfully within this gapless phase is given by the projection
\widehat{\mathbb{A}}\longrightarrow\widehat{H}
.
Recall that the category of genuine and non-genuine lines on the interface form the MTC

\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Vec}_{H}^{\omega})\,,

(B.36)

Among these there is
\mathsf{Rep}(H)
subcategory which are the genuine lines.

\mathcal{E}_{1}^{h}
are attached to
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{h}
in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}})
and
Q_{2}^{p(h)}
in
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{H/N})
.
Therefore after compactifying the interval occupied by
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}})
, only the lines
\mathcal{E}_{1}^{n}
get added to the 2-category of (genuine) defects on the boundary, meanwhile the remaining charged lines in
\mathcal{Z}(\mathsf{Vec}_{H}^{\omega})
are non-genuine lines attached to surfaces in the reduced TO.
Physically it means that the
\widehat{N}
is spontaneoulsy broken while the fate of the sub-symmetry
\widehat{H/N}
is undecided in the gapless phase.
In summary the boundary condition
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
is

\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathfrak{B}_{m}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{\text{DW}(H),\omega}}{(H/N)^{(1),\text{diag}}}\,,

(B.37)

The symmetry category on this boundary is

\mathcal{S}^{\prime}=\frac{2\mathsf{Rep}(H/N)\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{\text{DW}(H),\omega}}{(H/N)^{(1),\text{diag}}}\,.

(B.38)

The functor

\mathcal{F}:2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})\longrightarrow\mathcal{S}^{\prime}\,,

(B.39)

maps

\mathcal{F}(D_{1}^{\widehat{a}})=D_{1}^{\phi(\widehat{a})}\,,

(B.40)

where
\phi:\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}}\to\widehat{H}
and
D_{1}^{\phi(\widehat{a})}
is the topological Wilson line in
\mathfrak{T}_{\text{DW}(H),\omega}
that generates the
\widehat{H}
1-form symmetry.

In summary we have the following physical picture:
The UV theory has
\mathbb{A}^{(1)}=\widehat{\mathbb{A}}
symmetry.
The subgroup
\widehat{\mathbb{A}/H}
is trivial in this gapless phase,
and the remaining
\widehat{H}
acts faithfully.
In
\widehat{H}
,
\widehat{N}
is broken to the subgroup
\widehat{H/N}
, which survives in the reduced TO.

B.4.3
2\mathsf{Vec}_{({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)}}^{\beta}
Symmetry

More generally, gauging a subgroup
{\mathbb{B}}<{\mathbb{A}}
with discrete torsion
\nu\in H^{3}({\mathbb{B}},U(1))
on
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
, we obtain the symmetry
2\mathsf{Vec}_{({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)}}^{\beta}
, where
\beta
is defined by (
B.15
), on the symmetry boundary
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{B}}),\nu}
.

The lines that can end on both
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{B}}),\nu}
and
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\omega)}
are
{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}
for
\widehat{a}\in\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/({\mathbb{B}}H)}

29
29

29

\widehat{a}\in\widehat{A}
satisfies
\widehat{a}|_{\mathbb{B}}=1
and
\widehat{a}|_{H}=1
, i.e.,
\widehat{a}
is trivial on the product group
{\mathbb{B}}H
. They give rise to local operators
\mathcal{O}^{\widehat{a}}
after compactifying the
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}})
interval.
The surfaces that can end on both
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Neu}({\mathbb{B}}),\nu}
and
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\omega)}
are
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{n}
for
n\in{\mathbb{B}}\cap N
. They form line operators
\mathcal{L}^{n}
after compactifying the
\mathcal{Z}(2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}})
interval:

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}

{\bm{Q}}_{1}^{\widehat{a}}

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{n}

{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)}

.
Similarly,
\mathcal{O}^{\widehat{a}}
,

is charged non-trivially under

for
a\not\in{\mathbb{B}}H
, hence the 0-form symmetry
({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}
is broken to
(({\mathbb{B}}H)/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}
.
Hence the original symmetry
2\mathsf{Vec}_{({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)}}^{\beta}
is broken to
2\mathsf{Vec}_{({\mathbb{B}}H/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}\times({\mathbb{B}}/({\mathbb{B}}\cap N))^{(1)}}^{\beta}
.

The genuine line operator
\mathcal{L}^{n}
for
n\in{\mathbb{B}}\cap N
has
{\mathbb{B}}\cap N
fusion rule with non-trivial
F
-symbol specified by
\omega|_{{\mathbb{B}}\cap N}
. They are charged non-trivially under
D_{1}^{\widehat{a}}
for
\widehat{a}\in\widehat{A}
such that
\widehat{a}|_{{\mathbb{B}}\cap N}\neq 1

).
The
{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{hN}

{\bm{Q}}_{2}^{h}
for
h\in hN

\mathcal{E}_{1}^{h}

D_{2}^{h}

One can now determine the induced BC and symmetries on these. We will refrain from this as it has the potential to obscure matters (afterall we are discussing abelian group symmetries and their gauging). Nevertheless we will provide a summary of when in this instance there can be igSPT and igSSB phases later.

B.5
Criteria for igSPT and igSSB

Let us focus on some interesting cases of gapless phases, where the symmetry protects the criticality: igSPTs and igSSBs.
For abelian DW theories, we can provide criteria for the existence of such phases (for non-abelian groups these are more complicated and we provide examples in the main text).

A useful insight is the following:
when
N\neq H
and
\pi
is non-trivial, the partial order (
2.28
) tells us that a phase, determined by the interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
, can only flow to gapped phases
labeled by
H^{\prime}<H
and
\omega|_{H^{\prime}}
such that the 4-cocycle trivializes on
H^{\prime}/N
, i.e.,
\pi|_{H^{\prime}/N}=1
.
This will directly allow us to determine criteria for the igSPT and igSSB phases, i.e. when a given interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
and a given symmetry boundary can give rise to such a phase (once a suitable input phase transition is placed at the symmetry boundary).

2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}}
Symmetry.

Consider the 0-form symmetry
2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}}
. The number of vacua is determined by the number of bulk lines that can end on both
\mathfrak{B}_{\text{Dir}}
and the interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
, which in turn is determined by
H
. Hence a phase (either an SPT or an SSB) is intrinsically gapless whenever

\pi\neq 1\,.

(B.43)

This means that the reduced TO is a DW theory with a non-trivial twist.
Furthermore, the gapless phase associated to the interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
is a gSPT if
H={\mathbb{A}}
, otherwise it is a gSSB.
An example of a
2\mathsf{Vec}_{{\mathbb{A}}}
igSPT was provided in
[
43
]
for
{\mathbb{A}}={\mathbb{Z}}_{2}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{4}
and related to the “Cheshire charge” discussed in
[
89
]
. Condition (
B.43
) for intrinsically gapless phases for 0-form symmetry holds also for non-abelian groups and we will provide an example of a
D_{8}
igSPT in section
6
.

1-Form Symmetry
\mathbb{A}^{(1)}
.

Since
\mathcal{L}^{n}
,
n\in N
are charged non-trivially under the generators
D_{1}^{\widehat{a}}
,
\widehat{a}|_{N}\neq 1
, for the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})
symmetry, the
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})
symmetry is broken to
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}}/N)
. Hence only the interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
with
N=1
gives rise to an SPT phase, and it is a gapped phase iff
H=N=1
.

For
H\neq 1
and
N=1
, a gSPT phase determined by
\mathcal{I}_{(H,1,\omega,\pi)}
can always flow to the SPT determined by
\mathcal{I}_{(1,1,1,1)}
. There are no igSPT phases for
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})
symmetries. However, there can be instances of
igSSB
phases for
2\mathsf{Rep}(G)
symmetry, where
G
is non-abelian, for which we provide examples in sections
5
and
6
.

Similarly,
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\omega,\pi)}
determines a
gSSB
phase which can always flow to the SSB determined by
\mathcal{I}_{(N,N,\omega|_{N},1)}
, with the same symmetry breaking pattern. Hence there are no igSSB phases for
2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})
symmetries either.

2\mathsf{Vec}_{({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)}}^{\beta}
Symmetry.

For the 1-group symmetry we find the following:
Recall there are lines
\mathcal{L}^{n}
,
n\in{\mathbb{B}}\cap N
that break the 1-form symmetry
{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)}
to
({\mathbb{B}}/{\mathbb{B}}\cap N)^{(1)}
. Similarly, the presence of the local operators
\mathcal{O}^{\widehat{a}}
,
\widehat{a}\in\widehat{{\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}}H}
breaks the 0-form symmetry
({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}
to
({\mathbb{B}}H/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}
, i.e., the original symmetry
2\mathsf{Vec}_{({\mathbb{A}}/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}\times{\mathbb{B}}^{(1)}}^{\beta}
is broken to
2\mathsf{Vec}_{({\mathbb{B}}H/{\mathbb{B}})^{(0)}\times({\mathbb{B}}/{\mathbb{B}}\cap N)^{(1)}}^{\beta}
in the phase determined by an interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
.

Hence if both
{\mathbb{B}}H={\mathbb{A}}
and
{\mathbb{B}}\cap N=1
, the corresponding phase is a gSPT. Otherwise if
{\mathbb{B}}H\neq{\mathbb{A}}
or
{\mathbb{B}}\cap N\neq 1
, the phase is a gSSB.
Furthermore, such a phase is intrinsically gapless, if there is a subgroup
H^{\prime}<H
such that
\pi|_{H^{\prime}/N}=1
,
{\mathbb{B}}H^{\prime}={\mathbb{B}}H
and
{\mathbb{B}}\cap H^{\prime}={\mathbb{B}}\cap N
.

B.6
KT Transformations and Gapless Phases

To obtain a symmetric gapless (or gapped) phase, we simply complete the club quiche into a club sandwich by providing a gapless physical boundary condition. Operationally, this amounts to replacing
\mathfrak{B}_{e}
and
\mathfrak{B}_{m}
in the
\mathcal{S}
-symmetric BCs
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
by
H/N
0-form symmetric theory (gapped or gapless) and
\widehat{H/N}
1-form symmetric theory.
Concretely these theories take the following form:

•

For
\mathcal{S}=2\mathsf{Vec}_{\mathbb{A}}
, the phase that can be constructed from
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
is

\bigoplus_{x\in X}\left(\mathfrak{T}^{(0)}_{H/N}\right)_{x}\,,

(B.44)

where
\mathfrak{T}^{(0)}_{H/N}
is an
H/N
0-form symmetric CFT, with the action of
\mathcal{S}
same as on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
in (
B.29
).

•

For the 1-form symmetry
{\mathbb{A}}
, i.e.
\mathcal{S}=2\mathsf{Rep}({\mathbb{A}})
, the phase associated to the interface
\mathcal{I}_{(H,N,\pi,\omega)}
is

\frac{\mathfrak{T}^{(1)}_{\widehat{H/N}}\boxtimes\mathfrak{T}_{\text{DW}(H),\omega}}{(H/N)^{(1),\text{diag}}}\,,

(B.45)

where
\mathfrak{T}^{(1)}_{\widehat{H/N}}
is an
\widehat{H/N}
1-form symmetric CFT, with the action of
\mathcal{S}
same as on
\mathfrak{B}^{\prime}
in (
B.38
).

We can now use this to KT transform phases, from the smaller
(H/N)^{(0)}
and
(H/N)^{(1)}
etc symmetries to the larger ones, and thereby construct e.g. phase transitions (inputting the phase transition for the smaller symmetry).
